<h3 id="update-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» digestsMinDelay|body|integer|true|Minimum time in seconds to wait before sending an issue digest email.|
|» digestsMaxDelay|body|integer|true|Maximum time in seconds to wait before sending an issue digest email.|
|» securityToken|body|string|true|Token sent with security reports (CSP, Expect-CT, HPKP) so Sentry can verify their origin.|
|» securityTokenHeader|body|string|true|Name of the header carrying the security token on inbound security reports.|
|» isBookmarked|body|boolean|false|Enables starring the project within the projects tab. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» autofixAutomationTuning|body|string|false|How aggressively Seer runs Autofix on new issues. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.<br><br>* `off`<br>* `super_low`<br>* `low`<br>* `medium`<br>* `high`<br>* `always`|
|» seerScannerAutomation|body|boolean|false|Let Seer scan new issues automatically. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodSizeStatusChecksEnabled|body|boolean|false|Enable preprod size status checks. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodSizeStatusChecksRules|body|object|false|Rules controlling when preprod size status checks fail. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» preprodSizePrCommentsEnabled|body|boolean|false|Enable preprod size PR comments. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodSizePrCommentsRules|body|object|false|Rules controlling which preprod size changes are posted as PR comments. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» preprodSnapshotStatusChecksEnabled|body|boolean|false|Enable preprod snapshot status checks.|
|» preprodSnapshotStatusChecksFailOnAdded|body|boolean|false|Fail the preprod snapshot status check when snapshots are added.|
|» preprodSnapshotStatusChecksFailOnRemoved|body|boolean|false|Fail the preprod snapshot status check when snapshots are removed.|
|» preprodSnapshotStatusChecksFailOnChanged|body|boolean|false|Fail the preprod snapshot status check when snapshots change.|
|» preprodSnapshotStatusChecksFailOnRenamed|body|boolean|false|Fail the preprod snapshot status check when snapshots are renamed.|
|» preprodSizeEnabledByCustomer|body|boolean \| null|false|Enable preprod size analysis. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodDistributionEnabledByCustomer|body|boolean \| null|false|Enable preprod build distribution. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodDistributionPrCommentsEnabledByCustomer|body|boolean \| null|false|Post preprod distribution updates as PR comments. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodSnapshotPrCommentsEnabled|body|boolean \| null|false|Post preprod snapshot changes as PR comments.|
|» preprodSnapshotPrCommentsPostOnAdded|body|boolean \| null|false|Include added snapshots in preprod snapshot PR comments.|
|» preprodSnapshotPrCommentsPostOnRemoved|body|boolean \| null|false|Include removed snapshots in preprod snapshot PR comments.|
|» preprodSnapshotPrCommentsPostOnChanged|body|boolean \| null|false|Include changed snapshots in preprod snapshot PR comments.|
|» preprodSnapshotPrCommentsPostOnRenamed|body|boolean \| null|false|Include renamed snapshots in preprod snapshot PR comments.|
|» preprodSizeEnabledQuery|body|string \| null|false|Query selecting which preprod builds are size-analyzed. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» preprodDistributionEnabledQuery|body|string \| null|false|Query selecting which preprod builds are distributed. Can be updated with **`project:read`** permission.|
|» name|body|string|false|The name for the project|
|» slug|body|string|false|Uniquely identifies a project and is used for the interface.|
|» platform|body|string \| null|false|The platform for the project|
|» subjectPrefix|body|string|false|Custom prefix for emails from this project.|
|» subjectTemplate|body|string|false|The email subject to use (excluding the prefix) for individual alerts. Here are the list of variables you can use:<br>- `$title`<br>- `$shortID`<br>- `$projectID`<br>- `$orgID`<br>- `${tag:key}` - such as `${tag:environment}` or `${tag:release}`.|
|» resolveAge|body|integer \| null|false|Automatically resolve an issue if it hasn't been seen for this many hours. Set to `0` to disable auto-resolve.|
|» highlightContext|body|object|false|A JSON mapping of context types to lists of strings for their keys.<br>E.g. `{'user': ['id', 'email']}`|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» highlightTags|body|[string]|false|A list of strings with tag keys to highlight on this project's issues.<br>E.g. `['release', 'environment']`|
|» verifySSL|body|boolean|false|Verify SSL certificates when delivering outbound webhooks and service hooks.|
|» defaultEnvironment|body|string \| null|false|Environment selected by default when viewing this project.|
|» dataScrubber|body|boolean|false|Remove known sensitive values from events before storing them.|
|» dataScrubberDefaults|body|boolean|false|Also scrub Sentry's built-in list of sensitive field names.|
|» sensitiveFields|body|[string]|false|Additional field names to scrub from events, beyond the defaults.|
|» safeFields|body|[string]|false|Field names to exempt from scrubbing, including the built-in defaults.|
|» storeCrashReports|body|integer \| null|false|Number of native crash report files to store per issue. Use `-1` for unlimited or `0` to store none.|
|» relayPiiConfig|body|string \| null|false|Advanced data scrubbing rules, as a JSON string, applied before events are stored.|
|» builtinSymbolSources|body|[string]|false|Identifiers of Sentry-hosted symbol sources to use when symbolicating events.|
|» symbolSources|body|string \| null|false|Custom symbol sources, as a JSON string, to use when symbolicating events.|
|» enableNativeSourceServerMapping|body|boolean|false|Apply source server (srcsrv) information from native debug files to symbolicated frames.|
|» scrubIPAddresses|body|boolean|false|Discard client IP addresses rather than storing them on events.|
|» groupingConfig|body|string \| null|false|Identifier of the grouping algorithm used to assign events to issues.|
|» groupingEnhancements|body|string \| null|false|Grouping enhancement rules, as a newline-delimited config string, adjusting which stack frames contribute to an issue.|
|» fingerprintingRules|body|string \| null|false|Fingerprinting rules, as a newline-delimited config string, controlling how events are grouped into issues.|
|» secondaryGroupingConfig|body|string \| null|false|Grouping algorithm run alongside the primary one during a grouping migration.|
|» secondaryGroupingExpiry|body|integer \| null|false|Unix timestamp after which the secondary grouping algorithm stops running.|
|» scrapeJavaScript|body|boolean|false|Allow Sentry to fetch source files and source maps from your servers.|
|» enableAutoReleaseCreation|body|boolean|false|Automatically create releases from ingested events. When disabled, releases must be created manually (e.g. via the Sentry CLI).|
|» allowedDomains|body|[string]|false|Origins permitted to send events to this project. Use `*` to allow any.|
|» copy_from_project|body|integer|false|ID of a project whose settings, teams, and keys should be copied into this one.|
|» dynamicSamplingBiases|body|[object]|false|Per-bias toggles adjusting which transactions dynamic sampling favors retaining.|
|» » id|body|string|true|* `boostEnvironments`<br>* `boostKeyTransactions`<br>* `boostLatestRelease`<br>* `boostLowVolumeTransactions`<br>* `boostReplayId`<br>* `ignoreHealthChecks`<br>* `minimumSampleRate`<br>* `recalibrationRule`|
|» » active|body|boolean|false|none|
|» tempestFetchScreenshots|body|boolean|false|Fetch screenshots attached to console crash reports. Requires the Tempest feature.|
|» scmSourceContextEnabled|body|boolean|false|Enable on-demand source context fetching from SCM integrations for stack traces.|
|» debugFilesRole|body|string \| null|false|The role required to download debug information files, ProGuard mappings and source maps. If not set, inherits from organization setting.<br><br>* `member` - Member<br>* `admin` - Admin<br>* `manager` - Manager<br>* `owner` - Owner|

|» debugFilesRole|null|

<h3 id="update-a-project-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stats|[[integer]] \| object|false|none|Counts of non-transaction events per interval over the requested stats period, as [timestamp, count] pairs. Only included when a stats period is requested|
|» *anyOf*|[[integer]]|false|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[[integer]]|false|none|none|
|» *anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|integer|false|none|none|
|transactionStats|[[integer]]|false|none|Counts of transactions per interval over the requested stats period, as [timestamp, count] pairs. Only included when transaction stats are requested|
|sessionStats|object|false|none|Crash-free session rates for the current and previous stats period. Only included when session stats are requested|
|» currentCrashFreeRate|number(double) \| null|true|none|Crash-free rate in the current period, as a percentage. Null when there's no session data|
|» previousCrashFreeRate|number(double) \| null|true|none|Crash-free rate in the previous period, as a percentage. Null when there's no session data|
|» hasHealthData|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has release health (session) data|
|id|string|true|none|ID of the project|
|slug|string|true|none|Slug of the project|
|name|string|true|none|Name of the project|
|platform|string \| null|true|none|Platform of the project|
|dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|When the project was created (ISO 8601)|
|isBookmarked|boolean|true|none|Whether the requesting user bookmarked the project|
|isMember|boolean|true|none|Whether the requesting user is a member of a team with access to the project|
|features|[string]|true|none|Features enabled for the project|
|firstEvent|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the project received its first event (ISO 8601)|
|firstTransactionEvent|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent transactions|
|access|[string]|true|none|Scopes the requesting user has on the project through team membership and organization role|
|hasAccess|boolean|true|none|Whether the requesting user has access to the project|
|hasFeedbacks|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent user feedback|
|hasFlags|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent feature flags|
|hasMinifiedStackTrace|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent an event with a minified stack trace|
|hasMonitors|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has cron monitors|
|hasNewFeedbacks|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent user feedback from the user feedback widget|
|hasProfiles|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent profiles|
|hasReplays|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent replays|
|hasSessions|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent sessions|

## Delete a Project

<a id="opIddeleteProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/`

Schedules a project for deletion.

Deletion happens asynchronously and therefore is not immediate. However once deletion has
begun the state of a project changes and will be hidden from most public views.

<h3 id="delete-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|

<h3 id="delete-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## List a Project's CODEOWNERS Configurations

<a id="opIdlistProjectCodeOwners"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/codeowners/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/codeowners/`

Return the CODEOWNERS configurations for a project.

<h3 id="list-a-projects-codeowners-configurations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Optional fields to expand.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|expand|codeMapping|
|expand|ownershipSyntax|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "42",
    "raw": "src/* user@example.com",
    "dateCreated": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "dateUpdated": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "dateSynced": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
    "codeMappingId": "7",
    "provider": "github",
    "errors": {
      "missing_external_teams": [],
      "missing_external_users": [],
      "missing_user_emails": [],
      "teams_without_access": [],
      "users_without_access": []

    "schema": {

          "matcher": {

            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    "codeOwnersUrl": "https://github.com/example/repository/blob/main/CODEOWNERS"
  }
]
```

## Create a CODEOWNERS Configuration for a Project

<a id="opIdcreateProjectCodeOwners"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/codeowners/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "raw": "src/* user@example.com",
    "codeMappingId": "7"
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/codeowners/`

Create a CODEOWNERS configuration for a project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "raw": "src/* user@example.com",
  "codeMappingId": "7"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-codeowners-configuration-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» raw|body|string|true|The raw contents of the CODEOWNERS file.|
|» codeMappingId|body|string|true|The ID of the code mapping used to translate repository paths to stack trace paths.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "42",
  "raw": "src/* user@example.com",
  "dateCreated": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "dateUpdated": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "dateSynced": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "codeMappingId": "7",
  "provider": "github",
  "errors": {
    "missing_external_teams": [],
    "missing_external_users": [],
    "missing_user_emails": [],
    "teams_without_access": [],
    "users_without_access": []
  },
  "schema": {
    "$version": 1,
    "rules": [
      {
        "matcher": {
          "type": "codeowners",
          "pattern": "src/*"
        },
        "owners": [
          {
            "type": "user",
            "id": "1",
            "name": "user@example.com"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "codeOwnersUrl": "https://github.com/example/repository/blob/main/CODEOWNERS",
  "ownershipSyntax": "codeowners:src/* user@example.com\n"
}
```

```json
  }
```

<h3 id="list-a-projects-custom-inbound-filters-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="list-a-projects-custom-inbound-filters-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» id|string|true|read-only|The ID of the filter.|
|» dataType|string|true|none|The data the filter matches against. `all` is the catch-all: it filters every data type Sentry ingests, including ones added later, and accepts only the conditions that every data type carries a field for.<br><br>* `all`<br>* `error`<br>* `log`<br>* `metric`<br>* `span`|
|» conditions|[object]|true|none|Conditions are combined with AND: an event must match every condition to be filtered out. There is no OR between conditions, so e.g. two release conditions can express a range (`gte 2.0` and `lt 4.0`). To broaden matching, widen a condition's values or add separate filters.|
|» » type|string|true|none|The field the condition matches against. Every `dataType` accepts `release`, `environment` and `ip_address`. In addition, `error` accepts `error_type`, `error_message` and `geo_country_code`, `log` accepts `log_message`, and `metric` accepts `metric_name`. `span` and `all` accept no other types.<br><br>* `error_type`<br>* `error_message`<br>* `log_message`<br>* `metric_name`<br>* `release`<br>* `environment`<br>* `ip_address`<br>* `geo_country_code`|
|» » operator|string|false|none|How the field compares to `value`. `glob` matches the field against each value as a glob pattern. `equals`, `starts_with`, `contains` and `ends_with` match the field against each value case-insensitively, with every character read literally; `does_not_start_with`, `does_not_contain` and `does_not_end_with` match when the field is set and no value does. `cidr` matches `ip_address` against each value as an address or a CIDR range, and `not_cidr` matches when no value does. `gt`, `gte`, `lt` and `lte` compare one value as a version and only apply to `release`.<br><br>* `glob`<br>* `equals`<br>* `starts_with`<br>* `contains`<br>* `ends_with`<br>* `does_not_start_with`<br>* `does_not_contain`<br>* `does_not_end_with`<br>* `cidr`<br>* `not_cidr`<br>* `gt`<br>* `gte`<br>* `lt`<br>* `lte`|
|» » value|[string]|true|none|The values the field is compared to. The condition matches when any value matches, so multiple values act as OR; a negated operator matches when none does. A version comparison takes one release with a version such as `1.2.0` or `myapp@1.2.0`. A comparison with a package only applies to releases of that package.|
|» dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|read-only|When the filter was created.|
|» dateUpdated|string(date-time)|true|read-only|When the filter was last changed.|
|» legacyFilter|string \| null|true|read-only|Set on a filter that holds one of the filter lists of the project settings, to the id its outcomes are reported under. Such a filter keeps its data type and its one condition: only the name, the active flag and the condition values can change, and deleting it empties the list.|
|» name|string \| null|false|none|A human-readable label for the filter.|
|» active|boolean|false|none|Whether the filter drops matching data. An inactive filter is kept but ignored.|

|---|---|

|» dataType|error|
|» dataType|log|
|» dataType|metric|
|» dataType|span|

## Create a Custom Inbound Filter

<a id="opIdCreate a Custom Inbound Filter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/custom-inbound-filters/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "dataType": "all",
    "conditions": [
      {
        "type": "error_type",
        "operator": "glob",
        "value": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    ],
    "name": "string",
    "active": true
```

Create a custom inbound filter for a project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "dataType": "all",
  "conditions": [
    {
      "type": "error_type",
      "operator": "glob",
      "value": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "name": "string",
  "active": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-custom-inbound-filter-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» dataType|body|string|true|The data the filter matches against. `all` is the catch-all: it filters every data type Sentry ingests, including ones added later, and accepts only the conditions that every data type carries a field for.<br><br>* `all`<br>* `error`<br>* `log`<br>* `metric`<br>* `span`|
|» conditions|body|[object]|true|Conditions are combined with AND: an event must match every condition to be filtered out. There is no OR between conditions, so e.g. two release conditions can express a range (`gte 2.0` and `lt 4.0`). To broaden matching, widen a condition's values or add separate filters.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The field the condition matches against. Every `dataType` accepts `release`, `environment` and `ip_address`. In addition, `error` accepts `error_type`, `error_message` and `geo_country_code`, `log` accepts `log_message`, and `metric` accepts `metric_name`. `span` and `all` accept no other types.<br><br>* `error_type`<br>* `error_message`<br>* `log_message`<br>* `metric_name`<br>* `release`<br>* `environment`<br>* `ip_address`<br>* `geo_country_code`|
|» » operator|body|string|false|How the field compares to `value`. `glob` matches the field against each value as a glob pattern. `equals`, `starts_with`, `contains` and `ends_with` match the field against each value case-insensitively, with every character read literally; `does_not_start_with`, `does_not_contain` and `does_not_end_with` match when the field is set and no value does. `cidr` matches `ip_address` against each value as an address or a CIDR range, and `not_cidr` matches when no value does. `gt`, `gte`, `lt` and `lte` compare one value as a version and only apply to `release`.<br><br>* `glob`<br>* `equals`<br>* `starts_with`<br>* `contains`<br>* `ends_with`<br>* `does_not_start_with`<br>* `does_not_contain`<br>* `does_not_end_with`<br>* `cidr`<br>* `not_cidr`<br>* `gt`<br>* `gte`<br>* `lt`<br>* `lte`|
|» » value|body|[string]|true|The values the field is compared to. The condition matches when any value matches, so multiple values act as OR; a negated operator matches when none does. A version comparison takes one release with a version such as `1.2.0` or `myapp@1.2.0`. A comparison with a package only applies to releases of that package.|

## Assemble Debug Information Files

<a id="opIdassembleProjectDebugFiles"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/files/difs/assemble/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "property1": {
      "name": "string",
      "chunks": [
        "string"
      ],
      "debug_id": "string"
    },
    "property2": {
      "name": "string",
      "chunks": [
        "string"
      ],
      "debug_id": "string"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/files/difs/assemble/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Assemble previously uploaded chunks into debug information files.

The response reports each file's `state`, keyed by the same checksums. If chunks are
missing, upload them and send the request again. Repeat the request to poll until the
state is `ok` or `error`. Resending an identical request is safe: a file that is
already assembling or assembled reports its state instead of starting a new job.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "property1": {
    "name": "string",
    "chunks": [
      "string"
    ],
    "debug_id": "string"
  },
  "property2": {
    "name": "string",
    "chunks": [
      "string"
    ],
    "debug_id": "string"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="assemble-debug-information-files-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» **additionalProperties**|body|object|false|none|
|» » name|body|string|true|The file name. A ProGuard mapping without `debug_id` can carry it in the name, as in `/proguard/mapping-<uuid>.txt`.|
|» » chunks|body|[string]|true|The SHA-1 checksums of the file's chunks, in order. Upload missing chunks with the chunk upload endpoint. Send an empty list to poll the file's state.|
|» » debug_id|body|string|false|The debug ID to store the file under, overriding the one read from the file.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "property1": {
    "state": "string",
    "missingChunks": [
      "string"
    ],
    "detail": "string",
    "dif": {
      "id": "string",
      "uuid": "string",
      "debugId": "string",
      "codeId": "string",
      "cpuName": "string",
      "objectName": "string",
      "symbolType": "string",
      "headers": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "size": 0,
      "sha1": "string",
      "dateCreated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "data": {
        "type": "string",
        "features": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    }
  },
  "property2": {
    "state": "string",
    "missingChunks": [
      "string"
    ],
    "detail": "string",
    "dif": {
      "id": "string",
      "uuid": "string",
      "debugId": "string",
      "codeId": "string",
      "cpuName": "string",
      "objectName": "string",
      "symbolType": "string",
      "headers": {
        "property1": "string",
        "property2": "string"
      },
      "size": 0,
      "sha1": "string",
      "dateCreated": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "data": {
        "type": "string",
        "features": [
          "string"
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="assemble-debug-information-files-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="assemble-debug-information-files-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|» state|string|true|none|State of the file: ok, not_found, created, assembling or error|
|» missingChunks|[string]|true|none|Checksums of the chunks the server doesn't have yet|
|» detail|string \| null|false|none|Error message when the state is error|

|» » debugId|string|true|none|Debug ID of the file|
|» » codeId|string \| null|true|none|Code ID of the file, such as the GNU build ID. Null when the file has none|
|» » cpuName|string|true|none|CPU architecture of the file, such as x86_64 or arm64|
|» » objectName|string|true|none|Name of the object file|
|» » symbolType|string|true|none|Format of the file, such as macho, elf, pe, pdb, breakpad or proguard|
|» » headers|object|true|none|HTTP headers to download the file with, such as Content-Type|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|string|false|none|none|
|» » size|integer|true|none|Size of the file in bytes|
|» » sha1|string|true|none|SHA-1 checksum of the file|
|» » dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|When the file was uploaded (ISO 8601)|
|» » data|object|true|none|Extra data about the file, such as its features. Empty when not known|
|» » » type|string|false|none|Kind of the object, such as executable, debug companion or library. Left out for mapping files|
|» » » features|[string]|false|none|Debug features the file provides, such as symtab, debug, unwind, sources or mapping|

## Update an Inbound Data Filter

<a id="opIdupdateProjectFilter"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/filters/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "active": true,
    "subfilters": [
      "ie"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/filters/{filter_id}/`

Update various inbound data filters for a project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "active": true,
  "subfilters": [
    "ie"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-inbound-data-filter-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|filter_id|path|string|true|The type of filter toggle to update. The options are:<br>- `browser-extensions` - Filter out errors known to be caused by browser extensions.<br>- `localhost` - Filter out events coming from localhost. This applies to both IPv4 (``127.0.0.1``)<br>and IPv6 (``::1``) addresses.<br>- `filtered-transaction` - Filter out transactions for healthcheck and ping endpoints.<br>- `web-crawlers` - Filter out known web crawlers. Some crawlers may execute pages in incompatible<br>ways which cause errors that are unlikely to be seen by a normal user.<br>- `legacy-browser` - Filter out known errors from legacy browsers. Older browsers often give less<br>accurate information, and while they may report valid issues, the context to understand them is<br>incorrect or missing.<br>|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» active|body|boolean|false|Toggle the browser-extensions, localhost, filtered-transaction, or web-crawlers filter on or off.|
|» subfilters|body|[string]|false|<br>Specifies which legacy browser filters should be active. Anything excluded from the list will be<br>disabled. The options are:<br>- `ie` - Internet Explorer Version 11 and lower<br>- `edge` - Edge Version 110 and lower<br>- `safari` - Safari Version 15 and lower<br>- `firefox` - Firefox Version 110 and lower<br>- `chrome` - Chrome Version 110 and lower<br>- `opera` - Opera Version 99 and lower<br>- `android` - Android Version 3 and lower<br>- `opera_mini` - Opera Mini Version 34 and lower<br><br>Deprecated options:<br>- `ie_pre_9` - Internet Explorer Version 8 and lower<br>- `ie9` - Internet Explorer Version 9<br>- `ie10` - Internet Explorer Version 10<br>- `ie11` - Internet Explorer Version 11<br>- `safari_pre_6` - Safari Version 5 and lower<br>- `opera_pre_15` - Opera Version 14 and lower<br>- `opera_mini_pre_8` - Opera Mini Version 8 and lower<br>- `android_pre_4` - Android Version 3 and lower<br>- `edge_pre_79` - Edge Version 18 and lower (non Chromium based)<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» subfilters|ie|
|» subfilters|edge|
|» subfilters|safari|
|» subfilters|firefox|
|» subfilters|chrome|
|» subfilters|opera|
|» subfilters|android|
|» subfilters|opera_mini|
|» subfilters|ie_pre_9|
|» subfilters|ie9|
|» subfilters|ie10|
|» subfilters|ie11|
|» subfilters|opera_pre_15|
|» subfilters|android_pre_4|
|» subfilters|safari_pre_6|
|» subfilters|opera_mini_pre_8|
|» subfilters|edge_pre_79|

## Create a New Client Key

<a id="opIdcreateProjectKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/keys/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "rateLimit": {
      "count": 0,
      "window": 0
    },
    "useCase": "user"
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/keys/`

Create a new client key bound to a project.  The key's secret and public key
are generated by the server.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "rateLimit": {
    "count": 0,
    "window": 0
  },
  "useCase": "user"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-client-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string \| null|false|The optional name of the key. If not provided it will be automatically generated.|
|» rateLimit|body|object|false|Applies a rate limit to cap the number of errors accepted during a given time window. To<br>disable entirely set `rateLimit` to null.<br>```json<br>{<br>    "rateLimit": {<br>        "window": 7200, // time in seconds<br>        "count": 1000 // error cap<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » count|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » window|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» useCase|body|string|false|* `user`<br>* `profiling`<br>* `tempest`<br>* `demo`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» useCase|user|
|» useCase|profiling|
|» useCase|tempest|
|» useCase|demo|

## Update a Client Key

<a id="opIdupdateProjectKey"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/keys/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "isActive": true,
    "rateLimit": {
      "count": 0,
      "window": 0
    },
    "browserSdkVersion": "latest",
    "dynamicSdkLoaderOptions": {
      "hasReplay": true,
      "hasPerformance": true,
      "hasDebug": true,
      "hasFeedback": true,
      "hasLogsAndMetrics": true
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/keys/{key_id}/`

Update various settings for a client key.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "isActive": true,
  "rateLimit": {
    "count": 0,
    "window": 0
  },
  "browserSdkVersion": "latest",
  "dynamicSdkLoaderOptions": {
    "hasReplay": true,
    "hasPerformance": true,
    "hasDebug": true,
    "hasFeedback": true,
    "hasLogsAndMetrics": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-client-key-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|key_id|path|string|true|The ID of the key to update.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|The name for the client key|
|» isActive|body|boolean|false|Activate or deactivate the client key.|
|» rateLimit|body|object|false|Applies a rate limit to cap the number of errors accepted during a given time window. To<br>disable entirely set `rateLimit` to null.<br>```json<br>{<br>    "rateLimit": {<br>        "window": 7200, // time in seconds<br>        "count": 1000 // error cap<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » count|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» » window|body|integer \| null|false|none|
|» browserSdkVersion|body|string|false|The Sentry Javascript SDK version to use. The currently supported options are:<br><br>* `latest` - Most recent version<br>* `7.x` - Version 7 releases|
|» dynamicSdkLoaderOptions|body|object|false|Configures multiple options for the Javascript Loader Script.<br>- `Performance Monitoring`<br>- `Debug Bundles & Logging`<br>- `Session Replay` - Note that the loader will load the ES6 bundle instead of the ES5 bundle.<br>- `User Feedback` - Note that the loader will load the ES6 bundle instead of the ES5 bundle.<br>- `Logs and Metrics` - Note that the loader will load the ES6 bundle instead of the ES5 bundle. Requires SDK >= 10.0.0.<br>```json<br>{<br>    "dynamicSdkLoaderOptions": {<br>        "hasReplay": true,<br>        "hasPerformance": true,<br>        "hasDebug": true,<br>        "hasFeedback": true,<br>        "hasLogsAndMetrics": true<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » hasReplay|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » hasPerformance|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » hasDebug|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » hasFeedback|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » hasLogsAndMetrics|body|boolean|false|none|

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» browserSdkVersion|latest|
|» browserSdkVersion|7.x|

```json
  "projectId": 4505281256090153,

  "rateLimit": {
```

`GET /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/ownership/`

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json

  "raw": "path:src/views/checkout jane.smith@org.com \nurl:https://example.com/checkout jane.smith@org.com\ntags.transaction:/checkout/:page jane.smith@org.com",

  "lastUpdated": "2023-10-03T22:49:12.294741Z",

  "codeownersAutoSync": true,

          }
```

## Update Ownership Configuration for a Project

<a id="opIdupdateProjectOwnership"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/ownership/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "raw": "string",
    "fallthrough": true,
    "autoAssignment": "string",
    "codeownersAutoSync": true
  }'
```

`PUT /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/ownership/`

Updates ownership configurations for a project. Note that only the
attributes submitted are modified.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "raw": "string",
  "fallthrough": true,
  "autoAssignment": "string",
  "codeownersAutoSync": true
}
```

|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» raw|body|string|false|Raw input for ownership configuration. See the [Ownership Rules Documentation](/product/issues/ownership-rules/) to learn more.|
|» fallthrough|body|boolean|false|A boolean determining who to assign ownership to when an ownership rule has no match. If set to `True`, all project members are made owners. Otherwise, no owners are set.|
|» autoAssignment|body|string|false|Auto-assignment settings. The available options are:<br>- Auto Assign to Issue Owner<br>- Auto Assign to Suspect Commits<br>- Turn off Auto-Assignment|
|» codeownersAutoSync|body|boolean|false|Set to `True` to sync issue owners with CODEOWNERS updates in a release.|

|» » » type|string|true|none|Whether the owner is a user or a team|
|» » » name|string|true|none|Email of the user, or slug of the team|
|» » » id|string|false|none|ID of the user or team. Only set when the owner was resolved|
|raw|string \| null|true|none|Ownership rules as text|
|fallthrough|boolean|true|none|Whether issues that match no rule are assigned to all project members|
|dateCreated|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the ownership rules were created (ISO 8601)|
|lastUpdated|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the ownership rules were last updated (ISO 8601)|
|isActive|boolean|true|none|Whether the ownership rules are active|
|autoAssignment|string|true|none|Auto-assignment setting: Auto Assign to Suspect Commits, Auto Assign to Issue Owner or Turn off Auto-Assignment|
|codeownersAutoSync|boolean \| null|true|none|Whether CODEOWNERS files sync automatically when they change|

## List Repositories Linked to a Project

<a id="opIdlistProjectRepositories"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/repo/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/repo/`

List all repositories linked to a project.

Pass `?includeMappingCount=1` to include the number of code path mappings
per repository. Omitting it keeps the query cheaper for callers that
only need the list of connections.

<h3 id="list-repositories-linked-to-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|includeMappingCount|query|string|false|When set to `1`, each row includes a `mappingCount` field with the number of code path mappings for that repository. Omitted by default to keep the response lightweight.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "string",
    "integrationId": "string",
    "externalId": "string",
    "projectId": "string",
    "repositoryId": "string",
    "repoName": "string",
    "source": "string",
    "providerKey": "string",
    "mappingCount": 0
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-repositories-linked-to-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|

<h3 id="list-repositories-linked-to-a-project-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» id|string|true|none|ID of the link between the project and the repository|
|» integrationId|string \| null|true|none|ID of the repository's integration|
|» externalId|string \| null|true|none|ID of the repository in the provider|
|» projectId|string|true|none|ID of the project|
|» repositoryId|string|true|none|ID of the repository|
|» repoName|string|true|none|Name of the repository|
|» source|string|true|none|How the link was made: manual, scm_onboarding, auto_event, auto_name_match or seer_preference|
|» providerKey|string \| null|true|none|Key of the repository's provider, such as github|
|» mappingCount|integer|false|none|Number of code mappings between the project and the repository|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Link a Repository to a Project

<a id="opIdlinkProjectRepository"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/repo/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "repositoryId": 0
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/repo/`

Link a repository to a project. The repository must already exist
in the organization (connected via a VCS integration). Idempotent:
returns 200 if the link already exists, 201 if created.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repositoryId": 0
}
```

<h3 id="link-a-repository-to-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» repositoryId|body|integer|true|The ID of the repository to link.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "projectId": "string",
  "repositoryId": "string",
  "source": "string",
  "created": true
}
```

<h3 id="link-a-repository-to-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="link-a-repository-to-a-project-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|ID of the link between the project and the repository.|
|projectId|string|true|none|ID of the project.|
|repositoryId|string|true|none|ID of the repository.|
|source|string|true|none|How the link was made: manual, scm_onboarding, auto_event, auto_name_match or seer_preference.|
|created|boolean|true|none|Whether the request created the link. False when it already existed.|

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "repos": [
    {
      "repository_id": 0,
      "branch_name": "string",
      "instructions": "string",
      "branch_overrides": [

          "tag_name": "string",
          "tag_value": "string",
```

|body|body|object|true|none|
|» repos|body|[object]|true|Repositories to link and configure for Seer in this project.|

## Update a Project's Symbol Source

<a id="opIdupdateProjectSymbolSource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/symbol-sources/?id=string' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "http",
    "name": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "layout": {
      "type": "native",
      "casing": "lowercase"
    },
    "filters": {
      "filetypes": [
        "pe"
      ],
      "path_patterns": [
        "string"
      ],
      "requires_checksum": true
    },
    "url": "string",
    "username": "string",
    "password": "string",
    "bucket": "string",
    "region": "us-east-2",
    "access_key": "string",
    "secret_key": "string",
    "prefix": "string",
    "client_email": "string",
    "private_key": "string",
    "account": "string",
    "container": "string",
    "tenant_id": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "client_secret": "string"
  }'
```

`PUT /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/symbol-sources/`

Update a custom symbol source in a project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "http",
  "name": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "layout": {
    "type": "native",
    "casing": "lowercase"
  },
  "filters": {
    "filetypes": [
      "pe"
    ],
    "path_patterns": [
      "string"
    ],
    "requires_checksum": true
  },
  "url": "string",
  "username": "string",
  "password": "string",
  "bucket": "string",
  "region": "us-east-2",
  "access_key": "string",
  "secret_key": "string",
  "prefix": "string",
  "client_email": "string",
  "private_key": "string",
  "account": "string",
  "container": "string",
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "client_secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-projects-symbol-source-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|id|query|string|true|The ID of the source to update.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of the source.<br><br>* `http` - SymbolServer (HTTP)<br>* `gcs` - Google Cloud Storage<br>* `s3` - Amazon S3<br>* `azure` - Azure Blob Storage|
|» name|body|string|true|The human-readable name of the source.|
|» id|body|string|false|The internal ID of the source. Must be distinct from all other source IDs and cannot start with '`sentry:`'. If this is not provided, a new UUID will be generated.|
|» layout|body|object|false|Layout settings for the source. This is required for HTTP, GCS, and S3 sources.<br><br>**`type`** ***(string)*** - The layout of the folder structure. The options are:<br>- `native` - Platform-Specific (SymStore / GDB / LLVM)<br>- `symstore` - Microsoft SymStore<br>- `symstore_index2` - Microsoft SymStore (with index2.txt)<br>- `ssqp` - Microsoft SSQP<br>- `unified` - Unified Symbol Server Layout<br>- `debuginfod` - debuginfod<br>- `nnsymstore` - Nintendo Symbol Store<br><br>**`casing`** ***(string)*** - The layout of the folder structure. The options are:<br>- `default` - Default (mixed case)<br>- `uppercase` - Uppercase<br>- `lowercase` - Lowercase<br><br>```json<br>{<br>    "layout": {<br>        "type": "native"<br>        "casing": "default"<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » type|body|string|true|The source's layout type.<br><br>* `native`<br>* `symstore`<br>* `symstore_index2`<br>* `ssqp`<br>* `unified`<br>* `debuginfod`<br>* `slashsymbols`<br>* `nnsymstore`|
|» » casing|body|string|true|The source's casing rules.<br><br>* `lowercase`<br>* `uppercase`<br>* `default`|
|» filters|body|object|false|Filter settings for the source. This is optional for all sources.<br><br>**`filetypes`** ***(list)*** - A list of file types that can be found on this source. If this is left empty, all file types will be enabled. The options are:<br>- `pe` - Windows executable files<br>- `pdb` - Windows debug files<br>- `portablepdb` - .NET portable debug files<br>- `mach_code` - MacOS executable files<br>- `mach_debug` - MacOS debug files<br>- `elf_code` - ELF executable files<br>- `elf_debug` - ELF debug files<br>- `wasm_code` - WASM executable files<br>- `wasm_debug` - WASM debug files<br>- `breakpad` - Breakpad symbol files<br>- `sourcebundle` - Source code bundles<br>- `uuidmap` - Apple UUID mapping files<br>- `bcsymbolmap` - Apple bitcode symbol maps<br>- `il2cpp` - Unity IL2CPP mapping files<br>- `proguard` - ProGuard mapping files<br><br>**`path_patterns`** ***(list)*** - A list of glob patterns to check against the debug and code file paths of debug files. Only files that match one of these patterns will be requested from the source. If this is left empty, no path-based filtering takes place.<br><br>**`requires_checksum`** ***(boolean)*** - Whether this source requires a debug checksum to be sent with each request. Defaults to `false`.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>    "filters": {<br>        "filetypes": ["pe", "pdb", "portablepdb"],<br>        "path_patterns": ["*ffmpeg*"]<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » filetypes|body|[string]|false|The file types enabled for the source.|
|» » path_patterns|body|[string]|false|The debug and code file paths enabled for the source.|
|» » requires_checksum|body|boolean|false|Whether the source requires debug checksums.|
|» url|body|string|false|The source's URL. Optional for HTTP sources, invalid for all others.|
|» username|body|string|false|The user name for accessing the source. Optional for HTTP sources, invalid for all others.|
|» password|body|string|false|The password for accessing the source. Optional for HTTP sources, invalid for all others.|
|» bucket|body|string|false|The GCS or S3 bucket where the source resides. Required for GCS and S3 source, invalid for HTTP sources.|
|» region|body|string|false|The source's [S3 region](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/s3.html). Required for S3 sources, invalid for all others.<br><br>* `us-east-2` - US East (Ohio)<br>* `us-east-1` - US East (N. Virginia)<br>* `us-west-1` - US West (N. California)<br>* `us-west-2` - US West (Oregon)<br>* `ap-east-1` - Asia Pacific (Hong Kong)<br>* `ap-south-1` - Asia Pacific (Mumbai)<br>* `ap-northeast-2` - Asia Pacific (Seoul)<br>* `ap-southeast-1` - Asia Pacific (Singapore)<br>* `ap-southeast-2` - Asia Pacific (Sydney)<br>* `ap-northeast-1` - Asia Pacific (Tokyo)<br>* `ca-central-1` - Canada (Central)<br>* `cn-north-1` - China (Beijing)<br>* `cn-northwest-1` - China (Ningxia)<br>* `eu-central-1` - EU (Frankfurt)<br>* `eu-west-1` - EU (Ireland)<br>* `eu-west-2` - EU (London)<br>* `eu-west-3` - EU (Paris)<br>* `eu-north-1` - EU (Stockholm)<br>* `sa-east-1` - South America (São Paulo)<br>* `us-gov-east-1` - AWS GovCloud (US-East)<br>* `us-gov-west-1` - AWS GovCloud (US)|
|» access_key|body|string|false|The [AWS Access Key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/security-creds.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys).Required for S3 sources, invalid for all others.|
|» secret_key|body|string|false|The [AWS Secret Access Key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/security-creds.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys).Required for S3 sources, invalid for all others.|
|» prefix|body|string|false|The GCS, Azure or [S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-prefixes.html) prefix. Optional for GCS, Azure and S3 sources, invalid for HTTP.|
|» client_email|body|string|false|The GCS email address for authentication. Required for GCS sources, invalid for all others.|
|» private_key|body|string|false|The GCS private key. Required for GCS sources if not using impersonated tokens. Invalid for all others.|
|» account|body|string|false|The Azure storage account name. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|
|» container|body|string|false|The Azure blob container name. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|
|» tenant_id|body|string|false|The Microsoft Entra tenant ID. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|
|» client_id|body|string|false|The Microsoft Entra application (client) ID. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|The Microsoft Entra client secret. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|

## Add a Symbol Source to a Project

<a id="opIdaddProjectSymbolSource"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/symbol-sources/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "type": "http",
    "name": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "layout": {
      "type": "native",
      "casing": "lowercase"
    },
    "filters": {
      "filetypes": [
        "pe"
      ],
      "path_patterns": [
        "string"
      ],
      "requires_checksum": true
    },
    "url": "string",
    "username": "string",
    "password": "string",
    "bucket": "string",
    "region": "us-east-2",
    "access_key": "string",
    "secret_key": "string",
    "prefix": "string",
    "client_email": "string",
    "private_key": "string",
    "account": "string",
    "container": "string",
    "tenant_id": "string",
    "client_id": "string",
    "client_secret": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/symbol-sources/`

Add a custom symbol source to a project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "type": "http",
  "name": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "layout": {
    "type": "native",
    "casing": "lowercase"
  },
  "filters": {
    "filetypes": [
      "pe"
    ],
    "path_patterns": [
      "string"
    ],
    "requires_checksum": true
  },
  "url": "string",
  "username": "string",
  "password": "string",
  "bucket": "string",
  "region": "us-east-2",
  "access_key": "string",
  "secret_key": "string",
  "prefix": "string",
  "client_email": "string",
  "private_key": "string",
  "account": "string",
  "container": "string",
  "tenant_id": "string",
  "client_id": "string",
  "client_secret": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="add-a-symbol-source-to-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» type|body|string|true|The type of the source.<br><br>* `http` - SymbolServer (HTTP)<br>* `gcs` - Google Cloud Storage<br>* `s3` - Amazon S3<br>* `azure` - Azure Blob Storage|
|» name|body|string|true|The human-readable name of the source.|
|» id|body|string|false|The internal ID of the source. Must be distinct from all other source IDs and cannot start with '`sentry:`'. If this is not provided, a new UUID will be generated.|
|» layout|body|object|false|Layout settings for the source. This is required for HTTP, GCS, and S3 sources.<br><br>**`type`** ***(string)*** - The layout of the folder structure. The options are:<br>- `native` - Platform-Specific (SymStore / GDB / LLVM)<br>- `symstore` - Microsoft SymStore<br>- `symstore_index2` - Microsoft SymStore (with index2.txt)<br>- `ssqp` - Microsoft SSQP<br>- `unified` - Unified Symbol Server Layout<br>- `debuginfod` - debuginfod<br>- `nnsymstore` - Nintendo Symbol Store<br><br>**`casing`** ***(string)*** - The layout of the folder structure. The options are:<br>- `default` - Default (mixed case)<br>- `uppercase` - Uppercase<br>- `lowercase` - Lowercase<br><br>```json<br>{<br>    "layout": {<br>        "type": "native"<br>        "casing": "default"<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » type|body|string|true|The source's layout type.<br><br>* `native`<br>* `symstore`<br>* `symstore_index2`<br>* `ssqp`<br>* `unified`<br>* `debuginfod`<br>* `slashsymbols`<br>* `nnsymstore`|
|» » casing|body|string|true|The source's casing rules.<br><br>* `lowercase`<br>* `uppercase`<br>* `default`|
|» filters|body|object|false|Filter settings for the source. This is optional for all sources.<br><br>**`filetypes`** ***(list)*** - A list of file types that can be found on this source. If this is left empty, all file types will be enabled. The options are:<br>- `pe` - Windows executable files<br>- `pdb` - Windows debug files<br>- `portablepdb` - .NET portable debug files<br>- `mach_code` - MacOS executable files<br>- `mach_debug` - MacOS debug files<br>- `elf_code` - ELF executable files<br>- `elf_debug` - ELF debug files<br>- `wasm_code` - WASM executable files<br>- `wasm_debug` - WASM debug files<br>- `breakpad` - Breakpad symbol files<br>- `sourcebundle` - Source code bundles<br>- `uuidmap` - Apple UUID mapping files<br>- `bcsymbolmap` - Apple bitcode symbol maps<br>- `il2cpp` - Unity IL2CPP mapping files<br>- `proguard` - ProGuard mapping files<br><br>**`path_patterns`** ***(list)*** - A list of glob patterns to check against the debug and code file paths of debug files. Only files that match one of these patterns will be requested from the source. If this is left empty, no path-based filtering takes place.<br><br>**`requires_checksum`** ***(boolean)*** - Whether this source requires a debug checksum to be sent with each request. Defaults to `false`.<br><br>```json<br>{<br>    "filters": {<br>        "filetypes": ["pe", "pdb", "portablepdb"],<br>        "path_patterns": ["*ffmpeg*"]<br>    }<br>}<br>```|
|» » filetypes|body|[string]|false|The file types enabled for the source.|
|» » path_patterns|body|[string]|false|The debug and code file paths enabled for the source.|
|» » requires_checksum|body|boolean|false|Whether the source requires debug checksums.|
|» url|body|string|false|The source's URL. Optional for HTTP sources, invalid for all others.|
|» username|body|string|false|The user name for accessing the source. Optional for HTTP sources, invalid for all others.|
|» password|body|string|false|The password for accessing the source. Optional for HTTP sources, invalid for all others.|
|» bucket|body|string|false|The GCS or S3 bucket where the source resides. Required for GCS and S3 source, invalid for HTTP sources.|
|» region|body|string|false|The source's [S3 region](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/s3.html). Required for S3 sources, invalid for all others.<br><br>* `us-east-2` - US East (Ohio)<br>* `us-east-1` - US East (N. Virginia)<br>* `us-west-1` - US West (N. California)<br>* `us-west-2` - US West (Oregon)<br>* `ap-east-1` - Asia Pacific (Hong Kong)<br>* `ap-south-1` - Asia Pacific (Mumbai)<br>* `ap-northeast-2` - Asia Pacific (Seoul)<br>* `ap-southeast-1` - Asia Pacific (Singapore)<br>* `ap-southeast-2` - Asia Pacific (Sydney)<br>* `ap-northeast-1` - Asia Pacific (Tokyo)<br>* `ca-central-1` - Canada (Central)<br>* `cn-north-1` - China (Beijing)<br>* `cn-northwest-1` - China (Ningxia)<br>* `eu-central-1` - EU (Frankfurt)<br>* `eu-west-1` - EU (Ireland)<br>* `eu-west-2` - EU (London)<br>* `eu-west-3` - EU (Paris)<br>* `eu-north-1` - EU (Stockholm)<br>* `sa-east-1` - South America (São Paulo)<br>* `us-gov-east-1` - AWS GovCloud (US-East)<br>* `us-gov-west-1` - AWS GovCloud (US)|
|» access_key|body|string|false|The [AWS Access Key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/security-creds.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys).Required for S3 sources, invalid for all others.|
|» secret_key|body|string|false|The [AWS Secret Access Key](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/security-creds.html#access-keys-and-secret-access-keys).Required for S3 sources, invalid for all others.|
|» prefix|body|string|false|The GCS, Azure or [S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/using-prefixes.html) prefix. Optional for GCS, Azure and S3 sources, invalid for HTTP.|
|» client_email|body|string|false|The GCS email address for authentication. Required for GCS sources, invalid for all others.|
|» private_key|body|string|false|The GCS private key. Required for GCS sources if not using impersonated tokens. Invalid for all others.|
|» account|body|string|false|The Azure storage account name. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|

|» tenant_id|body|string|false|The Microsoft Entra tenant ID. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|

|» client_secret|body|string|false|The Microsoft Entra client secret. Required for Azure sources, invalid for all others.|

## List a Project's User Feedback

<a id="opIdList a Project's User Feedback"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/user-feedback/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/user-feedback/`

Return a list of user feedback items within this project.

*This list does not include submissions from the [User Feedback Widget](https://docs.sentry.io/product/user-feedback/#user-feedback-widget). This is because it is based on an older format called User Reports - read more [here](https://develop.sentry.dev/application/feedback-architecture/#user-reports). To return a list of user feedback items from the widget, please use the [issue API](https://docs.sentry.io/api/events/list-a-projects-issues/) with the filter `issue.category:feedback`.*

<h3 id="list-a-projects-user-feedback-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "comments": "It broke!",
    "dateCreated": "2018-11-06T21:20:11.468000Z",
    "email": "jane@example.com",
    "event": {
      "eventID": "14bad9a2e3774046977a21440ddb39b2",
      "id": "14bad9a2e3774046977a21440ddb39b2"
    },
    "eventID": "14bad9a2e3774046977a21440ddb39b2",
    "id": "1",
    "issue": null,
    "name": "Jane Smith",
    "user": null
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-a-projects-user-feedback-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="list-a-projects-user-feedback-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» id|string|true|none|ID of the feedback|
|» eventID|string|true|none|ID of the event the feedback is attached to|
|» name|string \| null|true|none|Name of the user who submitted the feedback. Falls back to the feedback's email address, then to the event user's name|
|» email|string \| null|true|none|Email address of the user who submitted the feedback. Falls back to the event user's email address|
|» comments|string|true|none|Comments the user submitted|
|» dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|When the feedback was submitted (ISO 8601)|
|» user|object \| null|true|none|User recorded on the feedback's event. Null when the event isn't found or has no user|
|» » id|string|true|none|ID of the user, as sent with the event|
|» » username|string \| null|true|none|Username sent with the event|
|» » email|string \| null|true|none|Email address sent with the event|
|» » name|string \| null|true|none|Display name of the user: the name, email address or username sent with the event, whichever is set first|
|» » ipAddress|string \| null|true|none|IP address sent with the event|
|» » avatarUrl|string \| null|true|none|Gravatar URL for the user's email address|
|» event|object|true|none|Event the feedback is attached to|
|» » id|string|true|none|ID of the event the feedback is attached to|
|» » eventID|string|true|none|ID of the event the feedback is attached to|
|» issue|object \| null|true|none|Issue the feedback's event belongs to. Null when the feedback isn't linked to an issue|
|» » isUnhandled|boolean|false|none|Whether the issue includes unhandled events|
|» » count|string|false|none|Total number of events in the issue|
|» » userCount|integer|false|none|Number of users affected by the issue|
|» » firstSeen|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the issue was first seen (ISO 8601)|
|» » lastSeen|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|When the issue was last seen (ISO 8601)|
|» » derivedData|object|false|none|Additional data derived for the issue. Only included when requested with expand|
|» » » blocker|string|true|none|Action that blocks progress on the issue: none, approve_root_cause, approve_plan, approve_code_changes or merge_pr|
|» » » progress|string|true|none|How far the issue is toward resolution: identified, assigned, diagnosed, fix_proposed or fix_applied|
|» » » status|string|true|none|Status of the issue from its action log: open or closed|
|» » » viewCount|integer|true|none|Number of times the issue was viewed|
|» » » hasOpenFixPr|boolean|true|none|Whether an open pull request is linked to the issue|
|» » » isAssigned|boolean|true|none|Whether the issue has an assignee|
|» » » hasRootCause|boolean|true|none|Whether a root cause was found for the issue|
|» » » lastCompletedAutofixStep|string|true|none|Furthest Autofix step completed: none, root_cause, solution, code_changes, pr_created or pr_iteration|
|» » » lastProgressedAt|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the issue's progress last advanced (ISO 8601)|
|» » » impact|object \| null|false|none|The issue's impact assessment, or null when no assessment is available|
|» » » » score|number(double) \| null|true|none|Estimated per-occurrence impact on the end user's capability from 0 to 100|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Submit User Feedback

<a id="opIdSubmit User Feedback"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/user-feedback/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "event_id": "14bad9a2e3774046977a21440ddb39b2",
    "name": "Jane Schmidt",
    "email": "jane@empowerplant.io",
    "comments": "It broke!"
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/user-feedback/`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

*This endpoint is DEPRECATED. We document it here for older SDKs and users who are still migrating to the [User Feedback Widget](https://docs.sentry.io/product/user-feedback/#user-feedback-widget) or [API](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/user-feedback/#user-feedback-api)(multi-platform). If you are a new user, do not use this endpoint - unless you don't have a JS frontend, and your platform's SDK does not offer a feedback API.*

Feedback must be received by the server no more than 30 minutes after the event was saved.

Additionally, within 5 minutes of submitting feedback it may also be overwritten. This is useful in situations where you may need to retry sending a request due to network failures.

If feedback is rejected due to a mutability threshold, a 409 status code will be returned.

Note: Feedback may be submitted with DSN authentication (see auth documentation).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "event_id": "14bad9a2e3774046977a21440ddb39b2",
  "name": "Jane Schmidt",
  "email": "jane@empowerplant.io",
  "comments": "It broke!"
}
```

<h3 id="submit-user-feedback-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|User's name.|
|» email|body|string(email)|true|User's email address.|
|» comments|body|string|true|Comments supplied by user.|
|» event_id|body|string|true|The event ID. This can be retrieved from the [beforeSend callback](https://docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/configuration/filtering/#using-beforesend).|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "comments": "It broke!",
  "dateCreated": "2018-11-06T21:20:11.468000Z",
  "email": "jane@example.com",
  "event": {
    "eventID": "14bad9a2e3774046977a21440ddb39b2",
    "id": "14bad9a2e3774046977a21440ddb39b2"
  },
  "eventID": "14bad9a2e3774046977a21440ddb39b2",
  "id": "1",
  "issue": null,
  "name": "Jane Smith",
  "user": null
}
```

<h3 id="submit-user-feedback-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Input|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|The requested resource does not exist|None|
|409|Conflict|Conflict|None|

## List a Project's Users

<a id="opIdlistProjectUsers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/users/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/users/`

Return a list of users seen within this project.

<h3 id="list-a-projects-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|query|query|string|false|Limit results to users matching the given query. Prefixes should be used to suggest the field to match on: `id`, `email`, `username`, `ip`. For example, `query=email:foo@example.com`.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "1",
    "tagValue": "email:sentry@example.com",
    "identifier": "1",
    "username": "sentry",
    "email": "sentry@example.com",
    "name": "Sentry",
    "ipAddress": "127.0.0.1",
    "avatarUrl": "https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/7ddf6ed64b36a1a28182f2c9af87c910?s=32",
    "hash": "7ddf6ed64b36a1a28182f2c9af87c910",
    "dateCreated": null
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-a-projects-users-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="list-a-projects-users-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» id|string \| null|true|none|ID of the legacy EventUser record. Null for users built from events|
|» tagValue|string \| null|true|none|Value of the user tag that matches the user, such as id:123 or email:jane@example.com|
|» identifier|integer \| string \| object \| null|true|none|ID the SDK sent for the user|
|» » *anyOf*|integer|false|none|none|
|» » *anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » *anyOf*|object \| null|false|none|none|
|» username|string \| null|true|none|Username the SDK sent for the user|
|» email|string \| null|true|none|Email address the SDK sent for the user|
|» name|string \| null|true|none|Display name of the user|
|» ipAddress|string \| null|true|none|IP address of the user|
|» avatarUrl|string|true|none|Gravatar URL of the user's email address|
|» hash|string \| null|true|none|MD5 hash of the first set user attribute: id, username, email or IP address|
|» dateCreated|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|Legacy field, always null|

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» » *anyOf*|null|

## Create a New Project

<a id="opIdcreateTeamProject"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/teams/string/string/projects/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "slug": "string",
    "platform": "string",
    "default_rules": true
  }'
```

`POST /teams/{organization_id_or_slug}/{team_id_or_slug}/projects/`

Create a new project bound to a team.

        Note: If your organization has disabled member project creation, the `org:write` scope or the Team Admin role on the team is required.
        

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "slug": "string",
  "platform": "string",
  "default_rules": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|team_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the team the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name for the project.|
|» slug|body|string \| null|false|Uniquely identifies a project and is used for the interface.<br>        If not provided, it is automatically generated from the name.|
|» platform|body|string \| null|false|The platform for the project.|
|» default_rules|body|boolean|false|<br>Defaults to true where the behavior is to alert the user on every new<br>issue. Setting this to false will turn this off and the user must create<br>their own alerts to be notified of new issues.<br>        |

|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

```json
  {
    "name": "mint_choco"

]
```

## Register a New Service Hook

<a id="opIdRegister a New Service Hook"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/hooks/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://empowerplant.io/sentry-hook",
    "events": [
      "event.alert",
      "event.created"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/hooks/`

Register a new service hook on a project.

Events include:

- event.alert: An alert is generated for an event (via rules).
- event.created: A new event has been processed.

This endpoint requires the 'servicehooks' feature to be enabled for your project.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "url": "https://empowerplant.io/sentry-hook",
  "events": [
    "event.alert",
    "event.created"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="register-a-new-service-hook-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the client keys belong to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the client keys belong to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» url|body|string|true|The URL for the webhook.|
|» events|body|[string]|true|The events to subscribe to.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "dateCreated": "2018-11-06T21:20:08.143Z",
  "events": [
    "event.alert",
    "event.created"
  ],
  "id": "4f9d73e63b7144ecb8944c41620a090b",
  "secret": "8fcac28aaa4c4f5fa572b61d40a8e084364db25fd37449c299e5a41c0504cbc2",
  "status": "active",
  "url": "https://empowerplant.io/sentry-hook"
}
```

<h3 id="register-a-new-service-hook-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Success|Inline|
|403|Forbidden|You do not have that feature enabled|None|
|404|Not Found|The requested resource does not exist|None|

<h3 id="register-a-new-service-hook-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|url|string|true|none|The URL that receives the service hook requests.|

## List Issue Views

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationIssueViews"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/group-search-views/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/group-search-views/`

Return the current organization member's issue views, with starred views first. Set
`createdBy=others` to list organization-visible views created by other members instead.

<h3 id="list-issue-views-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|createdBy|query|string|false|Whether to return issue views created by the current user or other members.<br><br>* `me`<br>* `others`|
|sort|query|[string]|false|The fields used to sort issue views, in order of precedence.|
|query|query|string|false|A case-insensitive search against issue view names and queries.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

|sort|popularity|

|sort|name|

|sort|created|
|sort|-created|
