## Create an Issue View

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationIssueView"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/group-search-views/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "string",
    "query": "string",
    "projects": [
      0
    ],
    "environments": [
      "string"
    ],
    "timeFilters": {
      "start": "string",
      "end": "string",
      "period": "string",
      "utc": true
    },
    "querySort": "date",
    "starred": true
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/group-search-views/`

Create a new custom view for the current organization member.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "string",
  "query": "string",
  "projects": [
    0
  ],
  "environments": [
    "string"
  ],
  "timeFilters": {
    "start": "string",
    "end": "string",
    "period": "string",
    "utc": true
  },
  "querySort": "date",
  "starred": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-an-issue-view-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» name|body|string|true|The name of the issue view.|
|» query|body|string|true|The issue search query. Issue search does not support the `AND`/`OR` boolean operators or parenthesized boolean groups. To match any of several values, use the list form instead: `issue:[PROJ-AB1, PROJ-CD2]`, `issue.priority:[high, medium]`.|
|» projects|body|[integer]|true|The project IDs included in the view. Use `-1` to include all projects.|
|» environments|body|[string]|true|The environment names included in the view. An empty list includes all environments.|
|» timeFilters|body|object|true|The time range for the view.|
|» » start|body|string \| null|false|The start of the time range in ISO-8601 format.|
|» » end|body|string \| null|false|The end of the time range in ISO-8601 format.|
|» » period|body|string \| null|false|The relative time period, such as `14d`.|
|» » utc|body|boolean \| null|false|Whether to interpret the time range as UTC.|
|» querySort|body|string|false|How to sort issues in the view.<br><br>* `date` - Last Seen<br>* `new` - First Seen<br>* `trends` - Trends<br>* `freq` - Events<br>* `user` - Users<br>* `inbox` - Date Added<br>* `recommended` - Recommended|
|» starred|body|boolean|false|Whether to star the issue view for the current user.|

|» querySort|new|
|» querySort|trends|

|» querySort|recommended|

## List an Organization's Issues

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationIssues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/issues/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/`

Return a list of issues for an organization. All parameters are supplied as query string parameters. A default query of `is:unresolved` is applied. To return all results, use an empty query value (i.e. ``?query=`). 

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|statsPeriodStart|query|string|false|How long ago the query period starts, in the same format as `statsPeriod`. Must be sent with `statsPeriodEnd`, and is ignored when `statsPeriod` is sent.|
|statsPeriodEnd|query|string|false|How long ago the query period ends, in the same format as `statsPeriod`. Must be sent with `statsPeriodStart`, and is ignored when `statsPeriod` is sent.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|groupStatsPeriod|query|string|false|The timeline on which stats for the groups should be presented.|
|shortIdLookup|query|string|false|If this is set to `1` then the query will be parsed for issue short IDs. These may ignore other filters (e.g. projects), which is why it is an opt-in.|
|query|query|string|false|An optional search query for filtering issues. A default query will apply if no query is set. For all results use this parameter with an empty string.|
|sort|query|string|false|The sort order of the view. Options include 'Last Seen' (`date`), 'First Seen' (`new`), 'Trends' (`trends`), 'Events' (`freq`), 'Users' (`user`), 'Date Added' (`inbox`), and 'Recommended' (`recommended`).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of issues to return. The maximum is 100.|
|expand|query|[string]|false|Additional data to include in the response.|
|collapse|query|[string]|false|Fields to remove from the response to improve query performance.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

## Bulk Mutate an Organization's Issues

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationIssues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/issues/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "inbox": true,
    "status": "resolved",
    "statusDetails": {
      "inNextRelease": true,
      "inRelease": "string",
      "inCommit": {
        "commit": "string",
        "repository": "string"
      },
      "ignoreDuration": 0,
      "ignoreCount": 0,
      "ignoreWindow": 0,
      "ignoreUserCount": 0,
      "ignoreUserWindow": 0
    },
    "substatus": "archived_until_escalating",
    "hasSeen": true,
    "isBookmarked": true,
    "isPublic": true,
    "isSubscribed": true,
    "merge": true,
    "discard": true,
    "assignedTo": "string",
    "priority": "low",
    "ignoreDuration": 0,
    "ignoreCount": 0,
    "ignoreWindow": 0,
    "ignoreUserCount": 0,
    "ignoreUserWindow": 0,
    "snoozeDuration": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/`

Bulk mutate various attributes on a maxmimum of 1000 issues. 
- For non-status updates, the `id` query parameter is required. 
- For status updates, the `id` query parameter may be omitted to update issues that match the filtering. 
If any IDs are out of scope, the data won't be mutated but the endpoint will still produce a successful response. For example, if no issues were found matching the criteria, a HTTP 204 is returned.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "inbox": true,
  "status": "resolved",
  "statusDetails": {
    "inNextRelease": true,
    "inRelease": "string",
    "inCommit": {
      "commit": "string",
      "repository": "string"
    },
    "ignoreDuration": 0,
    "ignoreCount": 0,
    "ignoreWindow": 0,
    "ignoreUserCount": 0,
    "ignoreUserWindow": 0
  },
  "substatus": "archived_until_escalating",
  "hasSeen": true,
  "isBookmarked": true,
  "isPublic": true,
  "isSubscribed": true,
  "merge": true,
  "discard": true,
  "assignedTo": "string",
  "priority": "low",
  "ignoreDuration": 0,
  "ignoreCount": 0,
  "ignoreWindow": 0,
  "ignoreUserCount": 0,
  "ignoreUserWindow": 0,
  "snoozeDuration": 0
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-mutate-an-organizations-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|id|query|[integer]|false|The list of issue IDs to mutate. It is optional for status updates, in which an implicit `update all` is assumed.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|query|query|string|false|An optional search query for filtering issues. A default query will apply if no query is set. For all results use this parameter with an empty string.|
|sort|query|string|false|The sort order of the view. Options include 'Last Seen' (`date`), 'First Seen' (`new`), 'Trends' (`trends`), 'Events' (`freq`), 'Users' (`user`), 'Date Added' (`inbox`), and 'Recommended' (`recommended`).|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» inbox|body|boolean|false|If true, marks the issue as reviewed by the requestor.|
|» status|body|string|false|The new status for the issues.<br><br>* `resolved`<br>* `unresolved`<br>* `ignored`<br>* `resolvedInNextRelease`<br>* `muted`|
|» statusDetails|body|object|false|Additional details about the resolution. Status detail updates that include release data are only allowed for issues within a single project.|
|» » inNextRelease|body|boolean|false|If true, marks the issue as resolved in the next release.|
|» » inRelease|body|string|false|The version of the release that the issue should be resolved in.If set to `latest`, the latest release will be used.|
|» » inCommit|body|object|false|The commit data that the issue should use for resolution.|
|» » » commit|body|string|true|The SHA of the resolving commit.|
|» » » repository|body|string|true|The name of the repository (as it appears in Sentry).|
|» » ignoreDuration|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until for this many minutes.|
|» » ignoreCount|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until it has occurred this many times in `ignoreWindow` minutes.|
|» » ignoreWindow|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until it has occurred `ignoreCount` times in this many minutes. (Max: 1 week)|
|» » ignoreUserCount|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until it has affected this many users in `ignoreUserWindow` minutes.|
|» » ignoreUserWindow|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until it has affected `ignoreUserCount` users in this many minutes. (Max: 1 week)|
|» substatus|body|string \| null|false|The new substatus of the issue.<br><br>* `archived_until_escalating`<br>* `archived_until_condition_met`<br>* `archived_forever`<br>* `escalating`<br>* `ongoing`<br>* `regressed`<br>* `new`|
|» hasSeen|body|boolean|false|If true, marks the issue as seen by the requestor.|
|» isBookmarked|body|boolean|false|If true, bookmarks the issue for the requestor.|
|» isPublic|body|boolean|false|If true, publishes the issue.|
|» isSubscribed|body|boolean|false|If true, subscribes the requestor to the issue.|
|» merge|body|boolean|false|If true, merges the issues together.|
|» discard|body|boolean|false|If true, discards the issues instead of updating them.|
|» assignedTo|body|string|false|The user or team that should be assigned to the issues. Values take the form of `<user_id>`, `user:<user_id>`, `<username>`, `<user_primary_email>`, or `team:<team_id>`.|
|» priority|body|string|false|The priority that should be set for the issues<br><br>* `low`<br>* `medium`<br>* `high`|
|» ignoreDuration|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue for this many minutes.|
|» ignoreCount|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until it is seen this many more times.|
|» ignoreWindow|body|integer|false|Window in minutes over which `ignoreCount` is measured. Maximum is 7 days.|
|» ignoreUserCount|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until it affects this many more users.|
|» ignoreUserWindow|body|integer|false|Window in minutes over which `ignoreUserCount` is measured. Maximum is 7 days.|
|» snoozeDuration|body|integer \| null|false|Snooze the issue for this many minutes.|

|» children|[string]|true|none|IDs of the issues that were merged into the parent issue|
|priority|string|false|none|New priority of the issues: high, medium or low|

|status|string|false|none|New status of the issues|
|statusDetails|object|false|none|Details of the new status, such as the release that resolves the issues or when an ignore expires|
|» inNextRelease|boolean|false|none|Whether the issues are resolved in the next release|
|» inRelease|string|false|none|Version of the release the issues are resolved in|
|» inCommit|object|false|none|Commit that resolves the issues|
|» » commit|string|true|none|SHA of the resolving commit|
|» » repository|string|true|none|Name of the repository the commit belongs to, as it appears in Sentry|
|» ignoreDuration|integer|false|none|Minutes the issues are ignored for|
|» ignoreCount|integer|false|none|Number of occurrences, within ignoreWindow minutes, after which the issues stop being ignored|
|» ignoreWindow|integer|false|none|Window in minutes for ignoreCount|
|» ignoreUserCount|integer|false|none|Number of affected users, within ignoreUserWindow minutes, after which the issues stop being ignored|
|» ignoreUserWindow|integer|false|none|Window in minutes for ignoreUserCount|
|subscriptionDetails|object|false|none|Why the requesting user is now subscribed to the issues|
|» disabled|boolean|false|none|Whether the requesting user turned off notifications for the issue|
|» reason|string|false|none|Why the requesting user is subscribed: commented, assigned, bookmarked, changed_status, mentioned or unknown|

## Bulk Remove an Organization's Issues

<a id="opIddeleteOrganizationIssues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/issues/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/`

Permanently remove the given issues. If IDs are provided, queries and filtering will be ignored. If any IDs are out of scope, the data won't be mutated but the endpoint will still produce a successful response. For example, if no issues were found matching the criteria, a HTTP 204 is returned.

<h3 id="bulk-remove-an-organizations-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|id|query|[integer]|false|The list of issue IDs to be removed. If not provided, it will attempt to remove the first 1000 issues.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|query|query|string|false|An optional search query for filtering issues. A default query will apply if no query is set. For all results use this parameter with an empty string.|
|sort|query|string|false|The sort order of the view. Options include 'Last Seen' (`date`), 'First Seen' (`new`), 'Trends' (`trends`), 'Events' (`freq`), 'Users' (`user`), 'Date Added' (`inbox`), and 'Recommended' (`recommended`).|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|sort|date|
|sort|freq|
|sort|inbox|
|sort|new|
|sort|recommended|
|sort|trends|
|sort|user|

## List a Project's Error Events

<a id="opIdlistProjectEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/events/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/events/`

Return a list of events bound to a project.

<h3 id="list-a-projects-error-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|statsPeriodStart|query|string|false|How long ago the query period starts, in the same format as `statsPeriod`. Must be sent with `statsPeriodEnd`, and is ignored when `statsPeriod` is sent.|
|statsPeriodEnd|query|string|false|How long ago the query period ends, in the same format as `statsPeriod`. Must be sent with `statsPeriodStart`, and is ignored when `statsPeriod` is sent.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|
|full|query|boolean|false|Specify true to include the full event body, including the stacktrace, in the event payload. When true, the page size is capped at 10.|
|sample|query|boolean|false|Return events in pseudo-random order. This is deterministic so an identical query will always return the same events in the same order.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» id|string|true|none|ID of the event|
|» event.type|string|true|none|Event type, such as error, default or transaction|
|» groupID|string \| null|true|none|ID of the issue the event belongs to|
|» eventID|string|true|none|ID of the event|
|» projectID|string|true|none|ID of the project the event belongs to|
|» message|string|true|none|Event message|
|» title|string|true|none|Event title|
|» location|string \| null|true|none|Source location of the event, such as a file and line|
|» culprit|string \| null|true|none|Function or module that caused the event|
|» user|object \| null|true|none|User context of the event|
|» » id|string \| null|false|none|ID the SDK sent for the user|
|» » email|string \| null|false|none|Email address of the user|
|» » username|string \| null|false|none|Username of the user|
|» » ip_address|string \| null|false|none|IP address of the user|
|» » name|string \| null|false|none|Name of the user|
|» » geo|object \| null|false|none|Location of the user, with keys such as country_code, city and region|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|string|false|none|none|
|» » data|object \| null|false|none|Extra data the SDK sent about the user|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|object|false|none|none|
|» tags|[object]|true|none|Tags attached to the event|
|» » query|string|false|none|Search query that matches this tag's user, such as user.email:"user@example.com". Only set for user tags|
|» » key|string|true|none|Tag key|
|» » value|string|true|none|Tag value|
|» platform|string \| null|true|none|Platform of the event, such as python or javascript|
|» dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|When the event occurred (ISO 8601)|
|» crashFile|string \| null|true|none|Crash report attachment of the event, if any|
|» metadata|object|true|none|Event metadata|
|» » title|string|false|none|Title of default and issue platform events|
|» » value|string|false|none|Exception value, or the subtitle of an issue|
|» » type|string|false|none|Exception type of error events|
|» » synthetic|boolean|false|none|Whether the SDK fabricated the exception to carry a stacktrace, so its type is a platform label rather than what went wrong|
|» » filename|string|false|none|File of the frame where the error happened|
|» » function|string|false|none|Function of the frame where the error happened|
|» » message|string|false|none|Message of default, security and feedback events|
|» » uri|string|false|none|URI that a CSP report blocked|
|» » directive|string|false|none|CSP directive that was violated|
|» » origin|string|false|none|Host name of HPKP, Expect-CT and Expect-Staple reports|
|» » name|string|false|none|Name of the person who sent user feedback|
|» » contact_email|string|false|none|Email of the person who sent user feedback|
|» » source|string|false|none|Where user feedback came from, such as a widget|
|» » in_app_frame_mix|string|false|none|Whether the stacktrace has in-app frames, system frames or both|
|» » stripped_crash|boolean|false|none|Whether a crash report was dropped because the issue already stores the most allowed|
|» » sdk|object|false|none|SDK of the issue's first event|
|» » » name|string|true|none|Name of the SDK, or unknown|
|» » » name_normalized|string|true|none|Name of the SDK, normalized for grouping|
|» » severity|number(double)|false|none|Severity score of the issue's first event|
|» » severity_reason|string|false|none|Why the severity score is what it is|
|» » initial_priority|integer|false|none|Priority the issue was created with|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve an Event for a Project

<a id="opIdgetProjectEvent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/events/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/events/{event_id}/`

Return details on an individual event.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-event-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|event_id|path|string|true|The ID of the event. It is a 32-character hexadecimal string as reported by the client.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|statsPeriodStart|query|string|false|How long ago the query period starts, in the same format as `statsPeriod`. Must be sent with `statsPeriodEnd`, and is ignored when `statsPeriod` is sent.|
|statsPeriodEnd|query|string|false|How long ago the query period ends, in the same format as `statsPeriod`. Must be sent with `statsPeriodStart`, and is ignored when `statsPeriod` is sent.|
|collapse|query|[string]|false|Parts of the response to skip computing. Specify `adjacentEvents` to skip looking up the neighboring events in the issue; `nextEventID` and `previousEventID` are then always `null`. Unknown values are ignored.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|collapse|adjacentEvents|

## List an Event's Attachments

<a id="opIdlistProjectEventAttachments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/events/string/attachments/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/events/{event_id}/attachments/`

Retrieve a list of attachments uploaded for a given event.

Requires the `event-attachments` organization feature.

<h3 id="list-an-events-attachments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|event_id|path|string|true|The ID of the event. It is a 32-character hexadecimal string as reported by the client.|
|query|query|string|false|Filter the attachments by name (substring match) or by attachment kind. Use `is:screenshot` to restrict the results to screenshot attachments.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
[
  {
    "id": "1234",
    "event_id": "9b29bbe17e9d4ee3a6d0fe9b2e8a3b1c",
    "type": "event.attachment",
    "name": "screenshot.png",
    "mimetype": "image/png",
    "dateCreated": "2026-04-15T18:22:31Z",
    "size": 248137,
    "headers": {
      "Content-Type": "image/png"
    },
    "sha1": "d3f299af02d6abbe92dd8368bab781824a9702ed"
  },
  {
    "id": "1235",
    "event_id": "9b29bbe17e9d4ee3a6d0fe9b2e8a3b1c",
    "type": "event.view_hierarchy",
    "name": "view-hierarchy.json",
    "mimetype": "application/json",
    "dateCreated": "2026-04-15T18:22:31Z",
    "size": 8421,
    "headers": {
      "Content-Type": "application/json"
    },
    "sha1": "fa0a5fad9e64129f6b5f60cca3a5b8c9b8a1a3a0"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="list-an-events-attachments-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="list-an-events-attachments-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» id|string|true|none|ID of the attachment|
|» event_id|string|true|none|ID of the event the attachment belongs to|
|» type|string|true|none|Type of the attachment, such as event.attachment or event.minidump|
|» name|string|true|none|File name of the attachment|
|» mimetype|string \| null|true|none|MIME type of the attachment|
|» dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|When the attachment was stored (ISO 8601)|
|» size|integer|true|none|Size of the attachment in bytes|
|» headers|object|true|none|Legacy field. Only contains Content-Type, which matches mimetype|
|» » **additionalProperties**|string \| null|false|none|none|
|» sha1|string \| null|true|none|Legacy field, always null|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve an Event Attachment

<a id="opIdgetProjectEventAttachment"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/events/string/attachments/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/events/{event_id}/attachments/{attachment_id}/`

Retrieve metadata for a single attachment on an event, or download its
contents by passing the `download` query parameter.

Requires the `event-attachments` organization feature.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-event-attachment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|event_id|path|string|true|The ID of the event. It is a 32-character hexadecimal string as reported by the client.|
|attachment_id|path|string|true|The numeric ID of the attachment, as returned from the attachments list endpoint.|
|download|query|string|false|If this parameter is present, the response will be a binary file download instead of JSON metadata. The value does not matter — any value (including empty) triggers the download. Depending on where the attachment is stored, the response may be a redirect to the storage service, so clients must follow redirects.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "1234",
  "event_id": "9b29bbe17e9d4ee3a6d0fe9b2e8a3b1c",
  "type": "event.attachment",
  "name": "screenshot.png",
  "mimetype": "image/png",
  "dateCreated": "2026-04-15T18:22:31Z",
  "size": 248137,
  "headers": {
    "Content-Type": "image/png"
  },
  "sha1": "d3f299af02d6abbe92dd8368bab781824a9702ed"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-an-event-attachment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="retrieve-an-event-attachment-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|ID of the attachment|
|event_id|string|true|none|ID of the event the attachment belongs to|
|type|string|true|none|Type of the attachment, such as event.attachment or event.minidump|
|name|string|true|none|File name of the attachment|
|mimetype|string \| null|true|none|MIME type of the attachment|
|dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|When the attachment was stored (ISO 8601)|
|size|integer|true|none|Size of the attachment in bytes|
|headers|object|true|none|Legacy field. Only contains Content-Type, which matches mimetype|
|» **additionalProperties**|string \| null|false|none|none|
|sha1|string \| null|true|none|Legacy field, always null|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Get Debug Information Related to Source Maps for a Given Event

<a id="opIdgetProjectEventSourceMapDebug"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/events/string/source-map-debug/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/events/{event_id}/source-map-debug/`

Return a list of source map errors for a given event.

<h3 id="get-debug-information-related-to-source-maps-for-a-given-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|event_id|path|string|true|The ID of the event. It is a 32-character hexadecimal string as reported by the client.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "dist": "1.0.0",
  "release": "frontend@1.0.0",
  "exceptions": [
    {
      "frames": [
        {
          "debug_id_process": {
            "debug_id": "f206e0e7-3d0c-41cb-bccc-11b716728e27",
            "uploaded_source_file_with_correct_debug_id": true,
            "uploaded_source_map_with_correct_debug_id": true
          },
          "release_process": {
            "abs_path": "https://example.com/static/js/main.js",
            "matching_source_file_names": [
              "~/static/js/main.js"
            ],
            "matching_source_map_name": "~/static/js/main.js.map",
            "source_map_reference": "main.js.map",
            "source_file_lookup_result": "found",
            "source_map_lookup_result": "found"
          },
          "scraping_process": {
            "source_file": {
              "url": "https://example.com/static/js/main.js",
              "status": "success"
            },
            "source_map": {
              "url": "https://example.com/static/js/main.js.map",
              "status": "success"
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "has_debug_ids": true,
  "min_debug_id_sdk_version": "7.56.0",
  "sdk_version": "7.60.0",
  "project_has_some_artifact_bundle": true,
  "release_has_some_artifact": true,
  "has_uploaded_some_artifact_with_a_debug_id": true,
  "sdk_debug_id_support": "full",
  "has_scraping_data": true
}
```

<h3 id="get-debug-information-related-to-source-maps-for-a-given-event-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="get-debug-information-related-to-source-maps-for-a-given-event-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|dist|string \| null|true|none|Distribution of the event|
|release|string \| null|true|none|Release of the event|
|exceptions|[object]|true|none|Source map debug results for each exception in the event|
|» frames|[object]|true|none|Source map debug results for each frame of the exception|
|» » debug_id_process|object|true|none|Results of resolving the frame with debug IDs|
|» » » debug_id|string \| null|true|none|Debug ID of the frame's source file. Null when the frame has none|
|» » » uploaded_source_file_with_correct_debug_id|boolean|true|none|Whether a source file with the frame's debug ID was uploaded|
|» » » uploaded_source_map_with_correct_debug_id|boolean|true|none|Whether a source map with the frame's debug ID was uploaded|
|» » release_process|object \| null|true|none|Results of resolving the frame with release artifacts. Null when the event has no release|
|» » » abs_path|string|true|none|Absolute path of the frame's file|

## List a Project's Issues

<a id="opIdList a Project's Issues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/issues/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/issues/`

<aside class="warning">
This operation is deprecated
</aside>

**Deprecated**: This endpoint has been replaced with the [Organization Issues endpoint](/api/events/list-an-organizations-issues/) which
supports filtering on project and additional functionality.

Return a list of issues (groups) bound to a project.  All parameters are supplied as query string parameters. 

 A default query of ``is:unresolved`` is applied. To return results with other statuses send an new query value (i.e. ``?query=`` for all results).

The ``statsPeriod`` parameter can be used to select the timeline stats which should be present. Possible values are: ``""`` (disable),``"24h"`` (default), ``"14d"``

User feedback items from the [User Feedback Widget](https://docs.sentry.io/product/user-feedback/#user-feedback-widget) are built off the issue platform, so to return a list of user feedback items for a specific project, filter for `issue.category:feedback`.

<h3 id="list-a-projects-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the issues belong to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the issues belong to.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|An optional stat period (can be one of `"24h"`, `"14d"`, and `""`), defaults to "24h" if not provided.|
|shortIdLookup|query|string|false|If this is set to `1` then short IDs are looked up by this function as well. This can cause the return value of the function to return an event issue of a different project which is why this is an opt-in.|
|query|query|string|false|An optional Sentry structured search query. If not provided an implied `"is:unresolved"` is assumed.|
|hashes|query|string|false|A list of hashes of groups to return. Is not compatible with 'query' parameter. The maximum number of hashes that can be sent is 100. If more are sent, only the first 100 will be used.|
|sort|query|string|false|The sort order of the issues. Options include 'Last Seen' (`date`), 'First Seen' (`new`), 'Trends' (`trends`), 'Events' (`freq`), 'Users' (`user`), and 'Recommended' (`recommended`).|
|limit|query|integer|false|The maximum number of issues to return. The maximum is 100.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|shortIdLookup|1|
|shortIdLookup|0|
|sort|date|
|sort|new|
|sort|trends|
|sort|freq|
|sort|user|
|sort|recommended|

## Bulk Mutate a List of Issues

<a id="opIdBulk Mutate a List of Issues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/issues/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "isPublic": false,
    "status": "unresolved"
  }'
```

`PUT /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/issues/`

Bulk mutate various attributes on issues.  The list of issues to modify is given through the `id` query parameter.  It is repeated for each issue that should be modified.

- For non-status updates, the `id` query parameter is required.
- For status updates, the `id` query parameter may be omitted
for a batch "update all" query.
- To restrict a batch "update all" to issues with a given status,
use the `query` parameter, e.g. `query=is:resolved`.

The following attributes can be modified and are supplied as JSON object in the body:

If any IDs are out of scope this operation will succeed without any data mutation.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "isPublic": false,
  "status": "unresolved"
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-mutate-a-list-of-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the issues belong to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the issues belong to.|
|id|query|integer|false|A list of IDs of the issues to be mutated. This parameter shall be repeated for each issue. It is optional only if a status is mutated in which case an implicit update all is assumed.|
|query|query|string|false|An optional Sentry structured search query that selects the issues to update when `id` is not provided. If not provided an implied `"is:unresolved"` is assumed. Use `is:<status>` (e.g. `is:resolved`) to limit it to issues with that status.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» status|body|string|false|The new status for the issues. Valid values are `"resolved"`, `"resolvedInNextRelease"`, `"unresolved"`, and `"ignored"`.|
|» statusDetails|body|object|false|Additional details about the resolution. Valid values are `"inRelease"`, `"inNextRelease"`, `"inCommit"`, `"ignoreDuration"`, `"ignoreCount"`, `"ignoreWindow"`, `"ignoreUserCount"`, and `"ignoreUserWindow"`.|
|» » inRelease|body|string|false|none|
|» » inNextRelease|body|boolean|false|none|
|» » inCommit|body|string|false|none|
|» » ignoreDuration|body|integer|false|none|
|» » ignoreCount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » ignoreWindow|body|integer|false|none|
|» » ignoreUserCount|body|integer|false|none|
|» » ignoreUserWindow|body|integer|false|none|
|» ignoreDuration|body|integer|false|The number of minutes to ignore this issue.|
|» isPublic|body|boolean|false|Sets the issue to public or private.|
|» merge|body|boolean|false|Allows to merge or unmerge different issues.|
|» assignedTo|body|string|false|The actor ID (or username) of the user or team that should be assigned to this issue.|
|» hasSeen|body|boolean|false|In case this API call is invoked with a user context this allows changing of the flag that indicates if the user has seen the event.|
|» isBookmarked|body|boolean|false|In case this API call is invoked with a user context this allows changing of the bookmark flag.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "isPublic": false,
  "status": "unresolved",
  "statusDetails": {}
}
```

<h3 id="bulk-mutate-a-list-of-issues-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Input|None|

## Bulk Remove a List of Issues

<a id="opIdBulk Remove a List of Issues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/issues/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/issues/`

Permanently remove the given issues. The list of issues to modify is given through the `id` query parameter.  It is repeated for each issue that should be removed.

If any IDs are out of scope this operation will succeed without any data mutation.

<h3 id="bulk-remove-a-list-of-issues-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the issues belong to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the issues belong to.|
|id|query|integer|false|A list of IDs of the issues to be removed. This parameter shall be repeated for each issue, e.g. `?id=1&id=2&id=3`. If this parameter is not provided, it will attempt to remove the first 1000 issues.|
|query|query|string|false|An optional Sentry structured search query that selects the issues to remove when `id` is not provided. If not provided an implied `"is:unresolved"` is assumed. Use `is:<status>` (e.g. `is:resolved`) to limit it to issues with that status.|

<h3 id="bulk-remove-a-list-of-issues-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|204|No Content|Success|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Project not found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

<h3 id="retrieve-an-issue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Update an Issue

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationIssue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/issues/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "inbox": true,
    "status": "resolved",
    "statusDetails": {
      "inNextRelease": true,
      "inRelease": "string",
      "inCommit": {
        "commit": "string",
        "repository": "string"
      },
      "ignoreDuration": 0,
      "ignoreCount": 0,
      "ignoreWindow": 0,
      "ignoreUserCount": 0,
      "ignoreUserWindow": 0
    },
    "substatus": "archived_until_escalating",
    "hasSeen": true,
    "isBookmarked": true,
    "isPublic": true,
    "isSubscribed": true,
    "merge": true,
    "discard": true,
    "assignedTo": "string",
    "priority": "low",
    "ignoreDuration": 0,
    "ignoreCount": 0,
    "ignoreWindow": 0,
    "ignoreUserCount": 0,
    "ignoreUserWindow": 0,
    "snoozeDuration": 0
  }'
```

`PUT /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/`

Update an individual issue's attributes. Only the attributes submitted
are modified.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "inbox": true,
  "status": "resolved",
  "statusDetails": {
    "inNextRelease": true,
    "inRelease": "string",
    "inCommit": {
      "commit": "string",
      "repository": "string"
    },
    "ignoreDuration": 0,
    "ignoreCount": 0,
    "ignoreWindow": 0,
    "ignoreUserCount": 0,
    "ignoreUserWindow": 0
  },
  "substatus": "archived_until_escalating",
  "hasSeen": true,
  "isBookmarked": true,
  "isPublic": true,
  "isSubscribed": true,
  "merge": true,
  "discard": true,
  "assignedTo": "string",
  "priority": "low",
  "ignoreDuration": 0,
  "ignoreCount": 0,
  "ignoreWindow": 0,
  "ignoreUserCount": 0,
  "ignoreUserWindow": 0,
  "snoozeDuration": 0
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» inbox|body|boolean|false|If true, marks the issue as reviewed by the requestor.|
|» status|body|string|false|The new status for the issues.<br><br>* `resolved`<br>* `unresolved`<br>* `ignored`<br>* `resolvedInNextRelease`<br>* `muted`|
|» statusDetails|body|object|false|Additional details about the resolution. Status detail updates that include release data are only allowed for issues within a single project.|
|» » inNextRelease|body|boolean|false|If true, marks the issue as resolved in the next release.|
|» » inRelease|body|string|false|The version of the release that the issue should be resolved in.If set to `latest`, the latest release will be used.|
|» » inCommit|body|object|false|The commit data that the issue should use for resolution.|
|» » » commit|body|string|true|The SHA of the resolving commit.|
|» » » repository|body|string|true|The name of the repository (as it appears in Sentry).|
|» » ignoreDuration|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until for this many minutes.|
|» » ignoreCount|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until it has occurred this many times in `ignoreWindow` minutes.|
|» » ignoreWindow|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until it has occurred `ignoreCount` times in this many minutes. (Max: 1 week)|
|» » ignoreUserCount|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until it has affected this many users in `ignoreUserWindow` minutes.|
|» » ignoreUserWindow|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until it has affected `ignoreUserCount` users in this many minutes. (Max: 1 week)|
|» substatus|body|string \| null|false|The new substatus of the issue.<br><br>* `archived_until_escalating`<br>* `archived_until_condition_met`<br>* `archived_forever`<br>* `escalating`<br>* `ongoing`<br>* `regressed`<br>* `new`|
|» hasSeen|body|boolean|false|If true, marks the issue as seen by the requestor.|
|» isBookmarked|body|boolean|false|If true, bookmarks the issue for the requestor.|
|» isPublic|body|boolean|false|If true, publishes the issue.|
|» isSubscribed|body|boolean|false|If true, subscribes the requestor to the issue.|
|» merge|body|boolean|false|If true, merges the issues together.|
|» discard|body|boolean|false|If true, discards the issues instead of updating them.|
|» assignedTo|body|string|false|The user or team that should be assigned to the issues. Values take the form of `<user_id>`, `user:<user_id>`, `<username>`, `<user_primary_email>`, or `team:<team_id>`.|
|» priority|body|string|false|The priority that should be set for the issues<br><br>* `low`<br>* `medium`<br>* `high`|
|» ignoreDuration|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue for this many minutes.|
|» ignoreCount|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until it is seen this many more times.|
|» ignoreWindow|body|integer|false|Window in minutes over which `ignoreCount` is measured. Maximum is 7 days.|
|» ignoreUserCount|body|integer|false|Ignore the issue until it affects this many more users.|
|» ignoreUserWindow|body|integer|false|Window in minutes over which `ignoreUserCount` is measured. Maximum is 7 days.|
|» snoozeDuration|body|integer \| null|false|Snooze the issue for this many minutes.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|resolved|
|» status|unresolved|
|» status|ignored|
|» status|resolvedInNextRelease|
|» status|muted|
|» substatus|archived_until_escalating|
|» substatus|archived_until_condition_met|
|» substatus|archived_forever|
|» substatus|escalating|
|» substatus|ongoing|
|» substatus|regressed|
|» substatus|new|
|» substatus|null|
|» priority|low|
|» priority|medium|
|» priority|high|

  "derivedData": {
    "blocker": "string",
    "progress": "string",

    "viewCount": 0,
    "hasOpenFixPr": true,
    "isAssigned": true,
    "hasRootCause": true,

    "impact": {
      "score": 0,
      "level": "super_low",
      "description": "string",
      "citations": [
        {

## Remove an Issue

<a id="opIddeleteOrganizationIssue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/issues/string/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/`

Asynchronously queue an individual issue for deletion.

<h3 id="remove-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|

<h3 id="remove-an-issue-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## List an Issue's Events

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationIssueEvents"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/issues/string/events/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/events/`

Return a list of events bound to an issue.

<h3 id="list-an-issues-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|statsPeriodStart|query|string|false|How long ago the query period starts, in the same format as `statsPeriod`. Must be sent with `statsPeriodEnd`, and is ignored when `statsPeriod` is sent.|
|statsPeriodEnd|query|string|false|How long ago the query period ends, in the same format as `statsPeriod`. Must be sent with `statsPeriodStart`, and is ignored when `statsPeriod` is sent.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|full|query|boolean|false|Specify true to include the full event body, including the stacktrace, in the event payload. When true, the page size is capped at 10.|
|sample|query|boolean|false|Return events in pseudo-random order. This is deterministic so an identical query will always return the same events in the same order.|
|query|query|string|false|An optional search query for filtering events. See [search syntax](https://docs.sentry.io/concepts/search/) and queryable event properties at [Sentry Search Documentation](https://docs.sentry.io/concepts/search/searchable-properties/events/) for more information. An example query might be `query=transaction:foo AND release:abc`|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Limit the number of rows to return in the result. Default and maximum allowed is 100.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

|» » synthetic|boolean|false|none|Whether the SDK fabricated the exception to carry a stacktrace, so its type is a platform label rather than what went wrong|
|» » filename|string|false|none|File of the frame where the error happened|
|» » function|string|false|none|Function of the frame where the error happened|
|» » message|string|false|none|Message of default, security and feedback events|
|» » uri|string|false|none|URI that a CSP report blocked|
|» » directive|string|false|none|CSP directive that was violated|
|» » origin|string|false|none|Host name of HPKP, Expect-CT and Expect-Staple reports|
|» » name|string|false|none|Name of the person who sent user feedback|
|» » contact_email|string|false|none|Email of the person who sent user feedback|
|» » source|string|false|none|Where user feedback came from, such as a widget|
|» » in_app_frame_mix|string|false|none|Whether the stacktrace has in-app frames, system frames or both|
|» » stripped_crash|boolean|false|none|Whether a crash report was dropped because the issue already stores the most allowed|
|» » sdk|object|false|none|SDK of the issue's first event|
|» » » name|string|true|none|Name of the SDK, or unknown|
|» » » name_normalized|string|true|none|Name of the SDK, normalized for grouping|
|» » severity|number(double)|false|none|Severity score of the issue's first event|
|» » severity_reason|string|false|none|Why the severity score is what it is|
|» » initial_priority|integer|false|none|Priority the issue was created with|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve an Issue Event

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationIssueEvent"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/issues/string/events/latest/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/events/{event_id}/`

Retrieves the details of an issue event.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-issue-event-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|event_id|path|string|true|The ID of the event to retrieve, or 'latest', 'oldest', or 'recommended'.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|statsPeriodStart|query|string|false|How long ago the query period starts, in the same format as `statsPeriod`. Must be sent with `statsPeriodEnd`, and is ignored when `statsPeriod` is sent.|
|statsPeriodEnd|query|string|false|How long ago the query period ends, in the same format as `statsPeriod`. Must be sent with `statsPeriodStart`, and is ignored when `statsPeriod` is sent.|
|collapse|query|[string]|false|Parts of the response to skip computing. Specify `adjacentEvents` to skip looking up the neighboring events in the issue; `nextEventID` and `previousEventID` are then always `null`. Unknown values are ignored.|
|llmFormat|query|string|false|If set, adds a `formatted` field to the response with the event rendered as the requested format for LLM consumption.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|event_id|latest|
|event_id|oldest|
|event_id|recommended|
|collapse|adjacentEvents|
|llmFormat|json|
|llmFormat|markdown|
|llmFormat|xml|

## List an Issue's Hashes

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationIssueHashes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/issues/string/hashes/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/hashes/`

List the hashes that make up an issue. Each hash represents a grouping
signature used to aggregate individual events into this issue.

<h3 id="list-an-issues-hashes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|full|query|boolean|false|Specify true to include the full event body, including the stacktrace, in the event payload. When true, the page size is capped at 10.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

## Retrieve Tag Details

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationIssueTag"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/issues/string/tags/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/tags/{key}/`

Return a list of values associated with this key for an issue. When paginated can return at most 1000 values.

<h3 id="retrieve-tag-details-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|issue_id|path|string|true|The ID of the issue you'd like to query.|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|key|path|string|true|The tag key to look the values up for.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "key": "flavors",
  "name": "Flavors",
  "uniqueValues": 2,
  "totalValues": 3,
  "topValues": [
    {
      "key": "strawberry",
      "name": "Strawberry",
      "value": "strawberry",
      "count": 2,
      "lastSeen": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "firstSeen": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    },
    {
      "key": "vanilla",
      "name": "Vanilla",
      "value": "vanilla",
      "count": 1,
      "lastSeen": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "firstSeen": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-tag-details-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="retrieve-tag-details-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|uniqueValues|integer \| null|false|none|Number of distinct values seen for the tag key|
|totalValues|integer \| null|false|none|Number of events counted for the tag key. For an issue tag, this is the issue's retained event count, including events without the tag|
|topValues|[object]|false|none|Most frequent values of the tag key, ordered by count|
|» query|string \| null|false|none|Search query that matches events with the tag value. Only set for the user tag|
|» key|string|true|none|Tag key, with the `sentry:` prefix removed from built-in keys|
|» name|string \| null|true|none|Display label of the tag value. For the user tag, the `id:`, `email:`, `username:` or `ip:` prefix is removed|
|» value|string \| null|true|none|Tag value|
|» count|integer \| null|true|none|Number of events with the tag value. Null for an empty value|
|» lastSeen|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the tag value was last seen (ISO 8601). Null for an empty value|
|» firstSeen|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the tag value was first seen (ISO 8601). Null for an empty value|
|key|string|true|none|Tag key, with the `sentry:` prefix removed from built-in keys|
|name|string|true|none|Display label of the tag key|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## List a Tag's Values for an Issue

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationIssueTagValues"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/issues/string/tags/string/values/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/issues/{issue_id}/tags/{key}/values/`

Returns a list of values associated with this key for an issue.
Returns at most 1000 values when paginated.

<h3 id="list-a-tags-values-for-an-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|key|path|string|true|The tag key to look the values up for.|
|sort|query|string|false|Sort order of the resulting tag values. Default is `id`.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|

## Retrieve a Shared Issue

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationSharedIssue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/shared/issues/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/shared/issues/{share_id}/`

Return an issue that was shared with a public link. This endpoint doesn't need
authentication: the share ID grants access.

The response holds less than the issue details endpoint, and its latest event
leaves out the user, tags, contexts, SDK, extra data, processing errors and
breadcrumbs.

Returns 404 when the share ID doesn't exist, when the issue belongs to another
organization, or when the organization turned off issue sharing.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-shared-issue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|share_id|path|string|true|The share ID of the issue, from its public share link.|

## Assemble an Artifact Bundle

<a id="opIdassembleOrganizationArtifactBundle"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/artifactbundle/assemble/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "projects": [
      "string"
    ],
    "checksum": "string",
    "chunks": [
      "string"
    ],
    "version": "string",
    "dist": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/artifactbundle/assemble/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Assemble previously uploaded chunks into an artifact bundle, such as source maps, and
store its debug IDs.

The response reports the bundle's `state`. If chunks are missing, upload them and send
the request again. Repeat the request to poll until the state is `ok` or `error`.
Resending an identical request is safe: a bundle that is already assembling or
assembled reports its state instead of starting a new job.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "projects": [
    "string"
  ],
  "checksum": "string",
  "chunks": [
    "string"
  ],
  "version": "string",
  "dist": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="assemble-an-artifact-bundle-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» projects|body|[string]|true|The IDs or slugs of the projects the bundle belongs to.|
|» checksum|body|string|true|The SHA-1 checksum of the whole bundle.|
|» chunks|body|[string]|true|The SHA-1 checksums of the bundle's chunks, in order. Upload missing chunks with the chunk upload endpoint. Send an empty list to poll the bundle's state.|
|» version|body|string|false|The release to associate the bundle with.|
|» dist|body|string|false|The distribution to associate the bundle with. Requires `version`.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "state": "string",
  "missingChunks": [
    "string"
  ],
  "detail": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="assemble-an-artifact-bundle-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="assemble-an-artifact-bundle-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|state|string|true|none|State of the bundle: ok, not_found, created, assembling or error|
|missingChunks|[string]|true|none|Checksums of the chunks the server doesn't have yet|
|detail|string \| null|false|none|Error message when the state is error|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve Statuses of Release Thresholds (Alpha)

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationReleaseThresholdStatuses"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/release-threshold-statuses/?start=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z&end=1970-01-01T00%3A00%3A00Z' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/release-threshold-statuses/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

List all derived statuses of releases that fall within the provided start/end datetimes.

Constructs a response key'd off \{`release_version`\}-\{`project_slug`\} that lists thresholds with their status for *specified* projects.
Each returned enriched threshold will contain the full serialized `release_threshold` instance as well as it's derived health statuses.

<h3 id="retrieve-statuses-of-release-thresholds-alpha-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|true|The start of the time series range as an explicit datetime, either in UTC ISO8601 or epoch seconds. Use along with `end`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|true|The inclusive end of the time series range as an explicit datetime, either in UTC ISO8601 or epoch seconds. Use along with `start`.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|A list of environment names to filter your results by.|
|projectSlug|query|[string]|false|A list of project slugs to filter your results by.|
|release|query|[string]|false|A list of release versions to filter your results by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|A list of project IDs or slugs to filter your results by.|

## List an Organization's Releases

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationReleases"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/releases/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/releases/`

Return a list of releases for a given organization, sorted by most recent.

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-releases-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|

## Create a New Release for an Organization

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationRelease"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/releases/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "version": "string",
    "projects": [
      "string"
    ],
    "ref": "string",
    "url": "http://example.com",
    "dateReleased": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "commits": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "repository": "string",
        "message": "string",
        "author_name": "string",
        "author_email": "string",
        "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "patch_set": [
          {
            "path": "string",
            "type": "s"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "status": "string",
    "owner": "string",
    "headCommits": [
      {
        "currentId": "string",
        "repository": "string",
        "previousId": "string"
      }
    ],
    "refs": [
      {
        "commit": "string",
        "repository": "string",
        "previousCommit": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/releases/`

Create a new release for the given organization. Releases are used by Sentry to
improve error reporting by correlating first-seen events with the release that may
have introduced them, and are required for source maps and other debug features.

Release versions that are the same across multiple projects within an organization
are treated as the same release in Sentry.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "version": "string",
  "projects": [
    "string"
  ],
  "ref": "string",
  "url": "http://example.com",
  "dateReleased": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "commits": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "repository": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "author_name": "string",
      "author_email": "string",
      "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "patch_set": [
        {
          "path": "string",
          "type": "s"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "status": "string",
  "owner": "string",
  "headCommits": [
    {
      "currentId": "string",
      "repository": "string",
      "previousId": "string"
    }
  ],
  "refs": [
    {
      "commit": "string",
      "repository": "string",
      "previousCommit": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-new-release-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» version|body|string|true|A version identifier for this release. Can be a version number, a commit hash, and so on.|
|» projects|body|[string]|true|A list of project slugs that are involved in this release.|
|» ref|body|string \| null|false|An optional commit reference. This is useful if a tagged version has been provided.|
|» url|body|string(uri) \| null|false|A URL that points to the release. For instance, this can be the path to an online interface to the source code, such as a GitHub URL.|
|» dateReleased|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|An optional date that indicates when the release went live.  If not provided the current time is used.|
|» commits|body|[object]|false|An optional list of commit data to be associated. Very long lists are truncated to the most recent commits.|
|» » id|body|string|true|none|
|» » repository|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » message|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » author_name|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » author_email|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » timestamp|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|
|» » patch_set|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » path|body|string|true|none|
|» » » type|body|string|true|none|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the release. Can be `open` or `archived`.|
|» owner|body|string|false|The username of the user to set as the release owner.|
|» headCommits|body|[object]|false|(Deprecated) Use `refs` instead. An optional list of head commits to associate with the release, one per repository.|
|» » currentId|body|string|true|none|
|» » repository|body|string|true|none|
|» » previousId|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» refs|body|[object]|false|An optional list of commit references, one per repository, used to associate commits with the release.|
|» » commit|body|string|true|none|
|» » repository|body|string|true|none|
|» » previousCommit|body|string \| null|false|none|

## Retrieve an Organization's Release

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationRelease"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/releases/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/releases/{version}/`

Return details on an individual release.

<h3 id="retrieve-an-organizations-release-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|version|path|string|true|The version identifier of the release|
|project_id|query|string|false|**Deprecated.** Deprecated. Use project instead.|
|project|query|integer \| string|false|The project ID or slug to filter by. Overrides project_id when both are sent.|
|health|query|boolean|false|Whether or not to include health data with the release. By default, this is false.|
|adoptionStages|query|boolean|false|Whether or not to include adoption stages with the release. By default, this is false.|
|summaryStatsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time used to query summary stats for the release. By default, this is 14d.|
|healthStatsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time used to query health stats for the release. By default, this is 24h if health is enabled.|
|sort|query|string|false|The field used to sort results by. By default, this is `date`.|
|status|query|string|false|Release statuses that you can filter by.|
|query|query|string|false|Filters results by using [query syntax](/product/sentry-basics/search/).<br><br>Example: `query=(transaction:foo AND release:abc) OR (transaction:[bar,baz] AND release:def)`<br>|

|status|open|

## Update an Organization's Release

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationRelease"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/releases/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ref": "string",
    "url": "http://example.com",
    "dateReleased": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "commits": [
      {
        "id": "string",
        "repository": "string",
        "message": "string",
        "author_name": "string",
        "author_email": "string",
        "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
        "patch_set": [
          {
            "path": "string",
            "type": "s"
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "status": "string",
    "headCommits": [
      {
        "currentId": "string",
        "repository": "string",
        "previousId": "string"
      }
    ],
    "refs": [
      {
        "commit": "string",
        "repository": "string",
        "previousCommit": "string"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/releases/{version}/`

Update a release. This can change some metadata associated with
the release (the ref, url, and dates).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ref": "string",
  "url": "http://example.com",
  "dateReleased": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "commits": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "repository": "string",
      "message": "string",
      "author_name": "string",
      "author_email": "string",
      "timestamp": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "patch_set": [
        {
          "path": "string",
          "type": "s"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "status": "string",
  "headCommits": [
    {
      "currentId": "string",
      "repository": "string",
      "previousId": "string"
    }
  ],
  "refs": [
    {
      "commit": "string",
      "repository": "string",
      "previousCommit": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-an-organizations-release-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|version|path|string|true|The version identifier of the release|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» ref|body|string \| null|false|An optional commit reference. This is useful if a tagged version has been provided.|
|» url|body|string(uri) \| null|false|A URL that points to the release. For instance, this can be the path to an online interface to the source code, such as a GitHub URL.|
|» dateReleased|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|An optional date that indicates when the release went live.  If not provided the current time is used.|
|» commits|body|[object]|false|An optional list of commit data to be associated. Very long lists are truncated to the most recent commits.|
|» » id|body|string|true|none|
|» » repository|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » message|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » author_name|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » author_email|body|string \| null|false|none|
|» » timestamp|body|string(date-time) \| null|false|none|
|» » patch_set|body|[object]|false|none|
|» » » path|body|string|true|none|
|» » » type|body|string|true|none|
|» status|body|string|false|The status of the release. Can be `open` or `archived`.|
|» headCommits|body|[object]|false|Deprecated, use `commits`. Head commits to associate with the release.|
