## Query Dropped and Accepted Events/Stats by Outcome and Reason

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationEventsDropped"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/events-dropped/?dataset=errors' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/events-dropped/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Return the events Sentry received but dropped (rate limited, filtered,
invalid, abuse, client discarded, cardinality limited) bucketed over the
requested interval, alongside the accepted volume per bucket so a caller
can compute the dropped share.

Select the dropped-data type with ``dataset`` and the bucket size with
``interval``. Optionally scope the dropped side to one classification with
``outcome`` (top-level) and/or ``reason`` (sub-classification within an
outcome); the accepted volume is always returned in full.

<h3 id="query-dropped-and-accepted-eventsstats-by-outcome-and-reason-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|dataset|query|string|true|Which dataset to query. The chosen dataset determines which fields are queryable.<br>- `errors` - Error events.<br>- `logs` - Structured log events.<br>- `profile_functions` - Function-level Profiling data.<br>- `spans` - Distributed tracing span events.<br>- `tracemetrics` - Application Metrics.<br>- `uptime_results` - Uptime monitoring check results.<br>|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|interval|query|integer \| string|false|The size of the bucket for the timeseries to have, must be a value smaller than the window being<br>queried. Either a number of seconds, or a number with a unit suffix of `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, or `w`, such as `5m` or<br>`1h`. If the interval is invalid a default interval will be selected instead|
|outcome|query|string|false|Narrow the dropped events (only) to a single top-level drop classification (e.g. `rate_limited`, `filtered`).<br><br>* `filtered`<br>* `rate_limited`<br>* `invalid`<br>* `abuse`<br>* `client_discard`<br>* `cardinality_limited`|
|reason|query|string|false|Narrow the dropped events to a single reason, the sub-classification within an outcome (e.g. `spike_protection` within `rate_limited`). Should be combined with `outcome`.|

## Query Explore Events in Timeseries Format

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationEventsTimeseries"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/events-timeseries/?dataset=errors' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/events-timeseries/`

Retrieves explore data for a given organization as a timeseries.

This endpoint can return timeseries for either 1 or many axis, and results grouped to the top events depending
on the parameters passed

**Note**: For queries extending past `30d`, spanning billions of rows, or running on projects with low
sample rates, the aggregation `yAxis=count_unique()` and filters on high-cardinality
fields (such as `query=user.id:bc`) will not return accurate results. Use these queries for rough
estimation only.

<h3 id="query-explore-events-in-timeseries-format-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|dataset|query|string|true|Which dataset to query. The chosen dataset determines which fields are queryable.<br>- `errors` - Error events.<br>- `logs` - Structured log events.<br>- `profile_functions` - Function-level Profiling data.<br>- `spans` - Distributed tracing span events.<br>- `tracemetrics` - Application Metrics.<br>- `uptime_results` - Uptime monitoring check results.<br>|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|topEvents|query|integer|false|The number of top event results to return, must be between 1 and 10.<br>When TopEvents is passed, both sort and groupBy are required parameters|
|comparisonDelta|query|integer|false|The delta in seconds to return additional offset timeseries by|
|interval|query|integer \| string|false|The size of the bucket for the timeseries to have, must be a value smaller than the window being<br>queried. Either a number of seconds, or a number with a unit suffix of `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, or `w`, such as `5m` or<br>`1h`. If the interval is invalid a default interval will be selected instead|
|sort|query|string|false|What to order the results of the query by. Must be something in the `field` list, excluding equations.|
|groupBy|query|[string]|false|List of fields to group by, *Required* for topEvents queries as this and sort determine what the<br>top events are|
|yAxis|query|[string]|false|The aggregate fields to create timeseries for, defaults to `count()` when<br>        not included. Pass the parameter more than once to get a timeseries for each aggregate, for<br>        example `?yAxis=count()&yAxis=p95(span.duration)`.<br>- `count()` - Total count of events over the period.<br>- `avg(field)` - Average value of the field over the period.<br>- `pXX(field)` - Percentile value of the field over the period. One of: `p50`, `p75`, `p90`, `p95`, `p99`, `p100`.<br>- `sum(field)` - Sum of all values for the field over the period.<br>- `min(field)` - Lowest value observed for the field over the period.<br>- `max(field)` - Highest value observed for the field over the period.<br>- `count_unique(field)` - Count of unique values observed for the field over the period. See *Note:* regarding accuracy on sampled data.<br>- `epm` - Average number of events received per minute.<br>- `eps` - Average number of events received per second.<br>- `failure_rate()` - Percentage of events whose `status` indicates failure.<br>- `failure_count()` - Total count of events with an error `status` over period.<br>- `performance_score(field)` - Web Vitals performance score for the selected measurement.<br>- `opportunity_score(field)` - Web Vitals opportunity score for the selected measurement.<br>|
|transformations[0]|query|[string]|false|Ordered transformations for a zero-based `yAxis` position. Replace `0` with the target axis index.<br>Repeat the indexed key for each operation, for example<br>`transformations[0]=fill(locf)&transformations[0]=smooth(sma,3)`.<br>Each axis accepts at most one fill and one smooth operation, in execution order.<br>Fill modes are `locf`, `zero`, and `linear`. Smoothing modes are `sma`, `ema`, and `asap`.<br>Omit the indexed key to leave that axis unchanged. Requires the interpolation and smoothing feature.|
|query|query|string|false|Filters results by using [query syntax](/concepts/search/).<br><br>Example: `query=(transaction:foo AND release:abc) OR (transaction:[bar,baz] AND release:def)`<br><br>With the `logs` dataset, a string attribute can also be matched against a regular expression written as `key://pattern//`, and excluded with `!key://pattern//`.<br>Patterns use [RE2 syntax](https://github.com/google/re2/wiki/Syntax), match anywhere in the value unless anchored with `^` or `$`, are case sensitive unless they start with `(?i)`, and are limited to 64 characters. A query can contain up to 16 regular expressions.<br>To search for a literal value that starts with `//`, quote it: `key:"//value"`.<br>See [regular expressions](/concepts/search/#regular-expressions-logs-only) for more details.<br><br>Example: `query=message://^Timeout after \d+ms//`<br>|
|disableAggregateExtrapolation|query|string|false|Whether to disable the use of extrapolation and return the sampled values, due to sampling the<br>number returned may be less than the actual values sent to Sentry|
|preventMetricAggregates|query|string|false|Whether to throw an error when aggregates are passed in the query or groupBy|
|excludeOther|query|string|false|Only applicable with TopEvents, whether to include the 'other' timeseries which represents all the<br>events that aren't in the top groups.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|dataset|errors|
|dataset|logs|
|dataset|profile_functions|
|dataset|spans|
|dataset|tracemetrics|
|dataset|uptime_results|
|disableAggregateExtrapolation|0|
|disableAggregateExtrapolation|1|
|preventMetricAggregates|0|
|preventMetricAggregates|1|
|excludeOther|0|
|excludeOther|1|

## Star a Service Span

<a id="opIdstarOrganizationServiceSpan"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/starred-service-spans/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "service_span": "string",
    "project_id": 1
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/starred-service-spans/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Star a service span for the requesting user. Span queries expose this as the
`is_starred_transaction` field. Returns `403` if the user has already starred
the service span.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "service_span": "string",
  "project_id": 1
}
```

<h3 id="star-a-service-span-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» service_span|body|string|true|The name of the service span to star or unstar.|
|» project_id|body|integer|true|The ID of the project the service span belongs to.|

|» count|number(double)|true|none|Number of data points of the metric in the time range|
|» lastSeen|number(double) \| null|true|none|When the metric was last seen, as a Unix timestamp. Null when not known|
|» context|object|false|none|Description of the metric. Only set when expand includes context|
|» » brief|string|false|none|Short description of the metric|
|» » details|[string]|false|none|Longer notes about the metric|

## Retrieve Trace Item Statistics

<a id="opIdRetrieve Trace Item Statistics"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/trace-items/stats/?statsType=attributeDistributions' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/trace-items/stats/`

Compute statistics, such as attribute value distributions, over the trace
items (spans or occurrences) matching the given query within the requested
time range.

<h3 id="retrieve-trace-item-statistics-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|statsType|query|[string]|true|The statistics to compute over the matching trace items.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|query|query|string|false|Sentry [search syntax](https://docs.sentry.io/concepts/search/) to filter trace items before computing statistics.|
|substringMatch|query|string|false|Restrict results to attribute names containing this substring (case-sensitive).|
|traceItemsLimit|query|integer|false|Maximum number of trace items to sample when computing statistics. Defaults to `1000`, which is also the maximum.|
|itemType|query|string|false|The trace item dataset to compute statistics for. Defaults to `spans`.<br><br>* `spans`<br>* `occurrences`|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|statsType|attributeDistributions|
|itemType|spans|
|itemType|occurrences|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "attributeDistributions": {
        "data": {
          "sentry.device": [
            {
              "label": "mobile",
              "value": 3
            },
            {
              "label": "desktop",
              "value": 1
            }
          ],
          "browser.name": [
            {
              "label": "chrome",
              "value": 3
            },
            {
              "label": "safari",
              "value": 1
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-trace-item-statistics-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="retrieve-trace-item-statistics-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[object]|true|none|Requested stats|
|» attributeDistributions|object|true|none|Value distributions of the attributes|
|» » data|object|true|none|Value distribution of each attribute, by attribute name|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|[object]|false|none|none|
|» » » » label|string|true|none|Value of the attribute|
|» » » » value|number(double)|true|none|Number of items with the value|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## List Logs for Traces or a Replay

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationTraceLogs"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/trace-logs/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/trace-logs/`

List the logs belonging to one or more traces, or to a replay, across all projects
in the organization the caller can access. A trace can span many projects, so the
`project` filter is ignored.

<h3 id="list-logs-for-traces-or-a-replay-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|traceId|query|[string]|false|The 32-character ID of a trace to list logs for. Can be repeated. At least one `traceId` or a `replayId` is required.|
|replayId|query|string|false|The 32-character ID of a replay to list logs for. Logs matching either a `traceId` or the `replayId` are returned.|
|query|query|string|false|Additional [search query](https://docs.sentry.io/concepts/search/) to filter the logs.|
|sort|query|[string]|false|Columns to sort by, prefixed with `-` for descending. Must be one of `id`, `project.id`, `trace`, `severity_number`, `severity`, `timestamp`, `timestamp_precise`, `message`. Defaults to `-timestamp` then `-timestamp_precise`.|
|timestamp|query|string|false|An ISO 8601 timestamp of an event in the trace. When passed, the query is narrowed to a window around this time, which is faster than searching the full time range.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|The number of logs to return per page, up to 9999.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "99083e5c2ee246be1242ee264d20fd58",
      "project.id": 4505281256090153,
      "trace": "a9f3c1e2b4d5467890abcdef12345678",
      "severity_number": 9,
      "severity": "INFO",
      "timestamp": "2026-09-01T12:00:00+00:00",
      "timestamp_precise": 1756728000123000000,
      "message": "Payment processed"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "fields": {
      "id": "string",
      "project.id": "string",
      "trace": "string",
      "severity_number": "integer",
      "severity": "string",
      "timestamp": "string",
      "timestamp_precise": "number",
      "message": "string"
    },
    "full_scan": true,
    "bytes_scanned": 255,
    "routingHint": "eyJ2IjogMSwgInRpZXIiOiAxfQ=="
  },
  "confidence": [
    {}
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-logs-for-traces-or-a-replay-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="list-logs-for-traces-or-a-replay-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[object]|true|none|The logs, sorted by the `sort` parameter|
|» id|string|true|none|The ID of the log|
|» project.id|integer|true|none|The ID of the project the log belongs to|
|» trace|string|true|none|The ID of the trace the log belongs to|
|» severity_number|integer|true|none|The OpenTelemetry severity number of the log, from 1 to 24, or 0 if unset|
|» severity|string|true|none|The severity text of the log, such as `info` or `error`|
|» timestamp|string(date-time)|true|none|When the log was recorded|
|» timestamp_precise|integer|true|none|When the log was recorded, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch|
|» message|string|true|none|The body of the log|
|meta|object|true|none|Metadata about the query and its fields|
|» fields|object|true|none|Type of each returned field, keyed by field name|
|» » **additionalProperties**|string|false|none|none|
|» full_scan|boolean|false|none|Whether the query scanned the full data set rather than a downsampled sample|
|» bytes_scanned|integer \| null|false|none|Number of bytes the query scanned, or null if it wasn't reported|
|» routingHint|string|false|none|Opaque routing hint of the query. Pass it unchanged as routing_hint when fetching the details of a log|
|confidence|[object]|true|none|Sampling confidence of each row in `data`, keyed by field. Logs are not aggregated, so each entry is an empty object|
|» **additionalProperties**|string \| null|false|none|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» **additionalProperties**|low|
|» **additionalProperties**|high|
|» **additionalProperties**|null|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

## Retrieve a Trace Item

<a id="opIdretrieveProjectTraceItem"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/trace-items/string/?trace_id=string&item_type=attachments' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/trace-items/{item_id}/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Retrieve a span, log or other trace item of a project, with all of its attributes.

Pass the `meta.routingHint` of the events response that listed the item as
`routing_hint`, unchanged. An invalid hint returns 400.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-trace-item-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|item_id|path|string|true|The hexadecimal ID of the item: the 16-character span ID for a span, or the 32-character item ID for other item types|
|trace_id|query|string|true|The 32-character ID of the trace the item belongs to|
|item_type|query|string|true|The type of the item|
|routing_hint|query|string|false|The opaque `meta.routingHint` of the events response that contained the item. Pass it unchanged to look the item up in the same storage. When it's omitted or empty, the default storage is used|
|timestamp|query|string(date-time)|false|When the item happened, as an ISO 8601 timestamp or Unix seconds. The lookup is narrowed to a few minutes around it, which makes it faster|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|item_type|attachments|
|item_type|logs|
|item_type|occurrences|
|item_type|preprod|
|item_type|processing_errors|
|item_type|profile_functions|
|item_type|spans|
|item_type|tracemetrics|
|item_type|uptime_results|

}

|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

## List an Organization's Custom Dashboards

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationDashboards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/dashboards/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/dashboards/`

Retrieve a list of custom dashboards that are associated with the given organization.

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-custom-dashboards-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|filter|query|[string]|false|Filter the dashboards returned. Repeat this parameter to apply multiple filters.|
|query|query|string|false|Filter dashboards by title.|
|sort|query|string|false|The property to sort results by. Prefix the value with `-` to sort in descending order.<br><br>Available fields are:<br>- `title`<br>- `dateCreated`<br>- `mostPopular`<br>- `recentlyViewed`<br>- `mydashboards`<br>- `myDashboardsAndRecentlyViewed`<br>|
|pin|query|string|false|Pin favorited dashboards to the top of the results.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Limit the number of rows to return in the result. Default and maximum allowed is 100.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|filter|excludeFavorites|
|filter|excludePrebuilt|
|filter|onlyFavorites|
|filter|onlyPrebuilt|
|filter|owned|
|filter|shared|
|filter|showHidden|
|pin|favorites|

## List a Custom Dashboard's Revisions

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationDashboardRevisions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/dashboards/0/revisions/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/revisions/`

Return the revision history of an organization's custom dashboard, newest first.

Each edit or restore of the dashboard records a revision holding the dashboard as it
was just before the change. Only the 10 most recent revisions are kept. Pass a
revision's `id` to the restore endpoint to roll the dashboard back to it.

<h3 id="list-a-custom-dashboards-revisions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|dashboard_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the dashboard you'd like to retrieve.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Limit the number of rows to return in the result. Default and maximum allowed is 100.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

> Example responses

    },

]

|» » avatarUrl|string \| null|true|none|URL of the avatar image, or null if none is set|
|» source|string|true|none|Change that recorded the revision, which holds the dashboard as it was just before that change: edit (a dashboard edit), edit-with-agent (an edit the client marked as made by an AI agent) or pre-restore (a restore of another revision)|

## Restore a Custom Dashboard Revision

<a id="opIdrestoreOrganizationDashboardRevision"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/dashboards/0/revisions/0/restore/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/dashboards/{dashboard_id}/revisions/{revision_id}/restore/`

Restore an organization's custom dashboard to the state saved in one of its revisions,
replacing its title, widgets and saved settings such as filters, and return the restored
dashboard.

The dashboard's current state is first recorded as a new revision with the source
`pre-restore`, so a restore can itself be undone. Restoring again records another
revision, so retrying a restore is not idempotent. The requesting user needs edit
access to the dashboard. Returns 400 if the revision can no longer be restored, for
example because its snapshot format is unsupported or it fails validation, and 409 if
another dashboard already uses the revision's title.

<h3 id="restore-a-custom-dashboard-revision-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|dashboard_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the dashboard you'd like to retrieve.|
|revision_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the dashboard revision, from the dashboard's revision list.|

## Retrieve Monitors for an Organization

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationMonitors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/monitors/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/monitors/`

Lists monitors, including nested monitor environments. May be filtered to a project or environment.

<h3 id="retrieve-monitors-for-an-organization-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|owner|query|string|false|The owner of the monitor, in the format `user:id` or `team:id`. May be specified multiple times.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

## Create a Monitor

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationMonitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/monitors/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "project": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "config": {
      "schedule_type": "crontab",
      "schedule": null,
      "checkin_margin": 1,
      "max_runtime": 1,
      "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
      "failure_issue_threshold": 1,
      "recovery_threshold": 1
    },
    "slug": "string",
    "status": "active",
    "owner": "string",
    "is_muted": true
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/monitors/`

Create a new monitor.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "project": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "config": {
    "schedule_type": "crontab",
    "schedule": null,
    "checkin_margin": 1,
    "max_runtime": 1,
    "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
    "failure_issue_threshold": 1,
    "recovery_threshold": 1
  },
  "slug": "string",
  "status": "active",
  "owner": "string",
  "is_muted": true
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-monitor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» project|body|string|true|The project ID or slug to associate the monitor to.|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the monitor. Used for notifications. If not set the slug will be derived from your monitor name.|
|» config|body|object|true|The configuration for the monitor.|
|» » schedule_type|body|string|false|Currently supports "crontab" or "interval"<br><br>* `crontab`<br>* `interval`|
|» » schedule|body|object|true|Varies depending on the schedule_type. Is either a crontab string, or a 2 element tuple for intervals (e.g. [1, 'day'])|
|» » checkin_margin|body|integer \| null|false|How long (in minutes) after the expected checkin time will we wait until we consider the checkin to have been missed.|
|» » max_runtime|body|integer \| null|false|How long (in minutes) is the checkin allowed to run for in CheckInStatus.IN_PROGRESS before it is considered failed. Maximum 10080 (7 days).|

|» timezone|string \| null|true|none|Timezone the schedule is evaluated in, as a tz database name|

|dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|When the monitor was created (ISO 8601)|

|» » previousCrashFreeRate|number(double) \| null|true|none|Crash-free rate in the previous period, as a percentage. Null when there's no session data|

## Retrieve a Monitor

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationMonitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/monitors/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/monitors/{monitor_id_or_slug}/`

Retrieves details for a monitor.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-monitor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|monitor_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the monitor.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|

|» » startingTimestamp|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the incident started (ISO 8601)|
|» » resolvingTimestamp|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the incident was resolved (ISO 8601)|
|» » brokenNotice|object \| null|true|none|Details of the broken monitor notice for the incident. Null when there's none|
|» » » userNotifiedTimestamp|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When users were notified that the monitor environment looks broken (ISO 8601)|
|» » » environmentMutedTimestamp|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the broken monitor environment was muted (ISO 8601)|
|owner|object \| null|true|none|Team or user that owns the monitor. Null when there's no owner|
|» type|string|true|none|Whether the actor is a user or a team|
|» id|string|true|none|ID of the user or team|
|» name|string|true|none|Display name of the user, or slug of the team|
|» email|string|false|none|Email address of the user. Only set for users|

## Update a Monitor

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationMonitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/monitors/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "project": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "config": {
      "schedule_type": "crontab",
      "schedule": null,
      "checkin_margin": 1,
      "max_runtime": 1,
      "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
      "failure_issue_threshold": 1,
      "recovery_threshold": 1
    },
    "slug": "string",
    "status": "active",
    "owner": "string",
    "is_muted": true
  }'
```

`PUT /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/monitors/{monitor_id_or_slug}/`

Update a monitor.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "project": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "config": {
    "schedule_type": "crontab",
    "schedule": null,
    "checkin_margin": 1,
    "max_runtime": 1,
    "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
    "failure_issue_threshold": 1,
    "recovery_threshold": 1
  },
  "slug": "string",
  "status": "active",
  "owner": "string",
  "is_muted": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-monitor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|monitor_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the monitor.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» project|body|string|true|The project ID or slug to associate the monitor to.|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the monitor. Used for notifications. If not set the slug will be derived from your monitor name.|
|» config|body|object|true|The configuration for the monitor.|
|» » schedule_type|body|string|false|Currently supports "crontab" or "interval"<br><br>* `crontab`<br>* `interval`|
|» » schedule|body|object|true|Varies depending on the schedule_type. Is either a crontab string, or a 2 element tuple for intervals (e.g. [1, 'day'])|
|» » checkin_margin|body|integer \| null|false|How long (in minutes) after the expected checkin time will we wait until we consider the checkin to have been missed.|
|» » max_runtime|body|integer \| null|false|How long (in minutes) is the checkin allowed to run for in CheckInStatus.IN_PROGRESS before it is considered failed. Maximum 10080 (7 days).|

|isMuted|boolean|true|none|Whether incidents are muted in all of the monitor's environments|
|isUpserting|boolean|true|none|Whether the most recent check-in was an upsert check-in|
|config|object|true|none|Configuration of the monitor|
|» schedule_type|string|true|none|Type of schedule: crontab or interval|
|» schedule|string \| [integer \| string]|true|none|Schedule of the monitor: a crontab string, or a [value, unit] pair for intervals, such as [1, "day"]|

|» *anyOf*|integer|false|none|none|
|» *anyOf*|string|false|none|none|

|» max_runtime|integer \| null|true|none|How long in minutes a check-in can stay in progress before it counts as failed|
|» timezone|string \| null|true|none|Timezone the schedule is evaluated in, as a tz database name|

|» recovery_threshold|integer \| null|true|none|Number of consecutive successful check-ins before the issue is resolved|

|dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|When the monitor was created (ISO 8601)|
|project|object|true|none|Project the monitor belongs to|

|» » previousCrashFreeRate|number(double) \| null|true|none|Crash-free rate in the previous period, as a percentage. Null when there's no session data|
|» » hasHealthData|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has release health (session) data|

## Delete a Monitor or Monitor Environments

<a id="opIddeleteOrganizationMonitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/monitors/string/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/monitors/{monitor_id_or_slug}/`

Delete a monitor or monitor environments.

<h3 id="delete-a-monitor-or-monitor-environments-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|monitor_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the monitor.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|

<h3 id="delete-a-monitor-or-monitor-environments-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Retrieve Check-Ins for a Monitor

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationMonitorCheckins"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/monitors/string/checkins/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

## Update a Monitor for a Project

<a id="opIdupdateProjectMonitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/monitors/string/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "project": "string",
    "name": "string",
    "config": {
      "schedule_type": "crontab",
      "schedule": null,
      "checkin_margin": 1,
      "max_runtime": 1,
      "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
      "failure_issue_threshold": 1,
      "recovery_threshold": 1
    },
    "slug": "string",
    "status": "active",
    "owner": "string",
    "is_muted": true
  }'
```

`PUT /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/monitors/{monitor_id_or_slug}/`

Update a monitor.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "project": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "config": {
    "schedule_type": "crontab",
    "schedule": null,
    "checkin_margin": 1,
    "max_runtime": 1,
    "timezone": "Africa/Abidjan",
    "failure_issue_threshold": 1,
    "recovery_threshold": 1
  },
  "slug": "string",
  "status": "active",
  "owner": "string",
  "is_muted": true
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-monitor-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|monitor_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the monitor.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» project|body|string|true|The project ID or slug to associate the monitor to.|
|» name|body|string|true|Name of the monitor. Used for notifications. If not set the slug will be derived from your monitor name.|
|» config|body|object|true|The configuration for the monitor.|
|» » schedule_type|body|string|false|Currently supports "crontab" or "interval"<br><br>* `crontab`<br>* `interval`|

<h3 id="update-a-monitor-for-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="update-a-monitor-for-a-project-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|ID of the monitor|
|name|string|true|none|Name of the monitor|
|slug|string|true|none|Slug that identifies the monitor in the organization|
|status|string|true|none|Status of the monitor. Disabled monitors don't accept check-ins|
|isMuted|boolean|true|none|Whether incidents are muted in all of the monitor's environments|
|isUpserting|boolean|true|none|Whether the most recent check-in was an upsert check-in|
|config|object|true|none|Configuration of the monitor|
|» schedule_type|string|true|none|Type of schedule: crontab or interval|
|» schedule|string \| [integer \| string]|true|none|Schedule of the monitor: a crontab string, or a [value, unit] pair for intervals, such as [1, "day"]|
|» » *anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» » *anyOf*|[integer \| string]|false|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[integer \| string]|false|none|none|
|» *anyOf*|integer|false|none|none|
|» *anyOf*|string|false|none|none|
|» checkin_margin|integer \| null|true|none|How long in minutes after the expected check-in time to wait before the check-in counts as missed|
|» max_runtime|integer \| null|true|none|How long in minutes a check-in can stay in progress before it counts as failed|
|» timezone|string \| null|true|none|Timezone the schedule is evaluated in, as a tz database name|
|» failure_issue_threshold|integer \| null|true|none|Number of consecutive missed or failed check-ins before an issue is created|
|» recovery_threshold|integer \| null|true|none|Number of consecutive successful check-ins before the issue is resolved|
|» alert_rule_id|integer \| null|true|none|ID of the alert rule linked to the monitor|
|dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|When the monitor was created (ISO 8601)|
|project|object|true|none|Project the monitor belongs to|
|» stats|[[integer]] \| object|false|none|Counts of non-transaction events per interval over the requested stats period, as [timestamp, count] pairs. Only included when a stats period is requested|
|» » *anyOf*|[[integer]]|false|none|none|
|*anonymous*|[[integer]]|false|none|none|
|» » *anyOf*|object|false|none|none|
|» » **additionalProperties**|integer|false|none|none|
|» transactionStats|[[integer]]|false|none|Counts of transactions per interval over the requested stats period, as [timestamp, count] pairs. Only included when transaction stats are requested|
|» sessionStats|object|false|none|Crash-free session rates for the current and previous stats period. Only included when session stats are requested|
|» » currentCrashFreeRate|number(double) \| null|true|none|Crash-free rate in the current period, as a percentage. Null when there's no session data|
|» » previousCrashFreeRate|number(double) \| null|true|none|Crash-free rate in the previous period, as a percentage. Null when there's no session data|
|» » hasHealthData|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has release health (session) data|
|» id|string|true|none|ID of the project|
|» slug|string|true|none|Slug of the project|
|» name|string|true|none|Name of the project|
|» platform|string \| null|true|none|Platform of the project|
|» dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|When the project was created (ISO 8601)|
|» isBookmarked|boolean|true|none|Whether the requesting user bookmarked the project|
|» isMember|boolean|true|none|Whether the requesting user is a member of a team with access to the project|
|» features|[string]|true|none|Features enabled for the project|
|» firstEvent|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the project received its first event (ISO 8601)|
|» firstTransactionEvent|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent transactions|
|» access|[string]|true|none|Scopes the requesting user has on the project through team membership and organization role|
|» hasAccess|boolean|true|none|Whether the requesting user has access to the project|
|» hasFeedbacks|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent user feedback|
|» hasFlags|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent feature flags|
|» hasMinifiedStackTrace|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent an event with a minified stack trace|
|» hasMonitors|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has cron monitors|
|» hasNewFeedbacks|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent user feedback from the user feedback widget|
|» hasProfiles|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent profiles|
|» hasReplays|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent replays|
|» hasSessions|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent sessions|
|» hasInsightsHttp|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent HTTP request spans used by Insights|
|» hasInsightsDb|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent database spans used by Insights|
|» hasInsightsAssets|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent asset spans used by Insights|
|» hasInsightsAppStart|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent app start spans used by Insights|
|» hasInsightsScreenLoad|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent screen load spans used by Insights|
|» hasInsightsVitals|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent web vitals spans used by Insights|
|» hasInsightsCaches|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent cache spans used by Insights|
|» hasInsightsQueues|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent queue spans used by Insights|
|» hasInsightsAgentMonitoring|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent AI agent spans used by Insights|
|» hasInsightsMCP|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent MCP spans used by Insights|
|» hasLogs|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent logs. Always true outside sentry.io|
|» hasTraceMetrics|boolean|true|none|Whether the project has sent trace metrics. Always true outside sentry.io|
|» isInternal|boolean|true|none|Whether this is the Sentry install's own internal project|
|» isPublic|boolean|true|none|Whether the project is public|
|» avatar|object|true|none|Avatar of the project. Always a letter avatar|
|» » avatarType|string|false|none|Avatar type|
|» » avatarUuid|string \| null|false|none|ID of the uploaded avatar image, or null|
|» » avatarUrl|string \| null|false|none|URL of the avatar image, or null if none is set|
|» color|string|true|none|Hex color code for the project, derived from its slug unless set explicitly|
|» status|string|true|none|Status of the project: active, deleted, or unknown|
|environments|[object]|true|none|Environments the monitor has received check-ins for|
|» name|string|true|none|Name of the environment|
|» status|string|true|none|Status of the monitor in the environment|
|» isMuted|boolean|true|none|Whether incidents are muted for the monitor in the environment|
|» dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|When the monitor was created (ISO 8601)|
|» lastCheckIn|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the most recent check-in was received, not counting missed check-ins (ISO 8601)|
|» nextCheckIn|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the next check-in is expected (ISO 8601)|
|» nextCheckInLatest|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|Latest time the next check-in can arrive before it counts as missed (ISO 8601)|
|» activeIncident|object \| null|true|none|Unresolved incident for the monitor in the environment. Null when there's none|
|» » startingTimestamp|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the incident started (ISO 8601)|
|» » resolvingTimestamp|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the incident was resolved (ISO 8601)|
|» » brokenNotice|object \| null|true|none|Details of the broken monitor notice for the incident. Null when there's none|
|» » » userNotifiedTimestamp|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When users were notified that the monitor environment looks broken (ISO 8601)|
|» » » environmentMutedTimestamp|string(date-time) \| null|true|none|When the broken monitor environment was muted (ISO 8601)|
|owner|object \| null|true|none|Team or user that owns the monitor. Null when there's no owner|
|» type|string|true|none|Whether the actor is a user or a team|
|» id|string|true|none|ID of the user or team|

## Delete a Monitor or Monitor Environments for a Project

<a id="opIddeleteProjectMonitor"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/projects/string/string/monitors/string/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /projects/{organization_id_or_slug}/{project_id_or_slug}/monitors/{monitor_id_or_slug}/`

Delete a monitor or monitor environments.

<h3 id="delete-a-monitor-or-monitor-environments-for-a-project-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the project the resource belongs to. Project slugs are unique within each organization.|
|monitor_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the monitor.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|

<h3 id="delete-a-monitor-or-monitor-environments-for-a-project-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|Accepted|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">

## Retrieve a Count of Replays for a Given Issue or Transaction

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationReplayCount"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/replay-count/?query=string&data_source=errors' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/replay-count/`

Return a count of replays for a list of issue or transaction IDs.

The `query` parameter is required. It is a search query that includes exactly one of `issue.id`, `transaction`, or `replay_id` (string or list of strings).

<h3 id="retrieve-a-count-of-replays-for-a-given-issue-or-transaction-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|query|query|string|true|Filters results by using [query syntax](/product/sentry-basics/search/).<br><br>Example: `query=(transaction:foo AND release:abc) OR (transaction:[bar,baz] AND release:def)`<br>|
|data_source|query|string|true|The data source to query replays from.<br><br>* `errors`<br>* `search_issues`<br>* `spans`|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The name of environments to filter by.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|The start of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|The end of the period of time for the query, expected in ISO-8601 format. For example, `2001-12-14T12:34:56.7890`.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|The period of time for the query, will override the start & end parameters, a number followed by one of:<br>- `d` for days<br>- `h` for hours<br>- `m` for minutes<br>- `s` for seconds<br>- `w` for weeks<br><br>For example, `24h`, to mean query data starting from 24 hours ago to now.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|project_id_or_slug|query|[string]|false|The legacy project slug filter. Prefer `project`, which accepts project IDs or slugs. Use `$all` to include all available projects. For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?projectSlug=$all`<br>- `/?projectSlug=android&projectSlug=javascript-react`<br>|
|returnIds|query|boolean|false|If true, return issue IDs rather than counts.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|data_source|errors|
|data_source|search_issues|
|data_source|spans|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "1": 9,
  "2": 0,
  "5": 0,
  "9": 1,
  "10": 29
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-a-count-of-replays-for-a-given-issue-or-transaction-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="retrieve-a-count-of-replays-for-a-given-issue-or-transaction-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|**additionalProperties**|integer|false|none|none|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:

</aside>

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/replay-selectors/`

Return a list of selectors for a given organization.

<h3 id="list-an-organizations-selectors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|statsPeriod|query|string|false|This defines the range of the time series, relative to now. The range is given in a `<number><unit>` format. For example `1d` for a one day range. Possible units are `m` for minutes, `h` for hours, `d` for days and `w` for weeks.You must either provide a `statsPeriod`, or a `start` and `end`.|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|This defines the start of the time series range as an explicit datetime, either in UTC ISO8601 or epoch seconds.Use along with `end` instead of `statsPeriod`.|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|This defines the inclusive end of the time series range as an explicit datetime, either in UTC ISO8601 or epoch seconds.Use along with `start` instead of `statsPeriod`.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|A list of project IDs or slugs to filter by.|
|projectSlug|query|[string]|false|A list of project slugs to filter your results by.|
|sort|query|string|false|The field to sort the output by.|
|sortBy|query|string|false|The field to sort the output by.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|The field to sort the output by.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Limit the number of rows to return in the result. Default and maximum allowed is 100.|
|query|query|string|false|Filters results by using [query syntax](/product/sentry-basics/search/).<br><br>Example: `query=(transaction:foo AND release:abc) OR (transaction:[bar,baz] AND release:def)`<br>|

## Retrieve a Replay Instance

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationReplay"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/replays/string/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/replays/{replay_id}/`

Return details on an individual replay.

<h3 id="retrieve-a-replay-instance-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|replay_id|path|string|true|The ID of the replay you'd like to retrieve. It is a 32-character hexadecimal string.|
|statsPeriod|query|string|false|<br>This defines the range of the time series, relative to now. The range is given in a<br>`<number><unit>` format. For example `1d` for a one day range. Possible units are `m` for<br>minutes, `h` for hours, `d` for days and `w` for weeks. You must either provide a<br>`statsPeriod`, or a `start` and `end`.<br>|
|start|query|string(date-time)|false|<br>This defines the start of the time series range as an explicit datetime, either in UTC<br>ISO8601 or epoch seconds. Use along with `end` instead of `statsPeriod`.<br>|
|end|query|string(date-time)|false|<br>This defines the inclusive end of the time series range as an explicit datetime, either in<br>UTC ISO8601 or epoch seconds. Use along with `start` instead of `statsPeriod`.<br>|
|field|query|[string]|false|Specifies a field that should be marshaled in the output. Invalid fields will be rejected.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|A list of project IDs or slugs to filter by.|
|projectSlug|query|[string]|false|A list of project slugs to filter your results by.|
|environment|query|[string]|false|The environments to filter by.|
|sort|query|string|false|The field to sort the output by.|
|sortBy|query|string|false|The field to sort the output by.|
|orderBy|query|string|false|The field to sort the output by.|

|queryReferrer|query|string|false|Internal referrer identifier used for query tracing.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Limit the number of rows to return in the result.|
|cursor|query|string|false|The cursor parameter is used to paginate results. See [here](https://docs.sentry.io/api/pagination/) for how to use this query parameter|

<h1 id="api-reference-spike-protection">Spike Protection</h1>

Endpoints for Spike Protection Notifications

<a href="https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-docs/issues/new/?title=API%20Documentation%20Error:%20/api/integration-platform/&amp;template=api_error_template.md">Found an error? Let us know.</a>

## List Spike Protection Notifications

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationNotificationsActions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/notifications/actions/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/notifications/actions/`

Returns all Spike Protection Notification Actions for an organization.

Notification Actions notify a set of members when an action has been triggered through a notification service such as Slack or Sentry.
For example, organization owners and managers can receive an email when a spike occurs.

You can use the `project` query parameter with project IDs or slugs to filter for certain projects.
A legacy project slug query parameter is also supported and takes priority if both are present.

<h3 id="list-spike-protection-notifications-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|project_id_or_slug|query|[string]|false|The legacy project slug filter. Prefer `project`, which accepts project IDs or slugs. Use `$all` to include all available projects. For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?projectSlug=$all`<br>- `/?projectSlug=android&projectSlug=javascript-react`<br>|
|triggerType|query|string|false|Type of the trigger that causes the notification. The only supported value right now is: `spike-protection`|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 836501735,
  "organizationId": 62848264,
  "integrationId": null,
  "sentryAppId": null,
  "serviceType": "sentry_notification",
  "targetDisplay": "default",
  "targetIdentifier": "default",
  "targetType": "specific",
  "triggerType": "spike-protection",
  "projects": [
    4505321021243392
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="list-spike-protection-notifications-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|

<h3 id="list-spike-protection-notifications-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|integer|true|none|ID of the notification action|
|organizationId|integer|true|none|ID of the organization|
|integrationId|integer \| null|true|none|ID of the integration that sends the notification. Null when none is used|
|sentryAppId|integer \| null|true|none|ID of the Sentry app that receives the notification. Null when none is used|
|projects|[integer]|true|none|IDs of the projects the action applies to|
|serviceType|string \| null|true|none|Service that sends the notification, such as email, slack or pagerduty|
|triggerType|string|true|none|What triggers the action, such as audit-log or spike-protection|
|targetType|string \| null|true|none|Kind of target: specific, user, team, sentry_app or issue_owners|
|targetIdentifier|string \| null|true|none|ID of the target in the service, such as a Slack channel ID|
|targetDisplay|string \| null|true|none|Name of the target, such as #alerts|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Create a Spike Protection Notification Action

<a id="opIdcreateOrganizationNotificationsAction"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/notifications/actions/' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "trigger_type": "string",
    "service_type": "string",
    "integration_id": 0,
    "target_identifier": "string",
    "target_display": "string",
    "projects": [
      "string"
    ],
    "sentry_app_id": 0,
    "target_type": "specific"
  }'
```

`POST /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/notifications/actions/`

Creates a new Notification Action for Spike Protection.

Notification Actions notify a set of members when an action has been triggered through a notification service such as Slack or Sentry.
For example, organization owners and managers can receive an email when a spike occurs.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "trigger_type": "string",
  "service_type": "string",
  "integration_id": 0,
  "target_identifier": "string",
  "target_display": "string",
  "projects": [
    "string"
  ],
  "sentry_app_id": 0,
  "target_type": "specific"
}
```

<h3 id="create-a-spike-protection-notification-action-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» trigger_type|body|string|true|Type of the trigger that causes the notification. The only supported trigger right now is: `spike-protection`.|
|» service_type|body|string|true|Service that is used for sending the notification.<br>- `email`<br>- `slack`<br>- `sentry_notification`<br>- `pagerduty`<br>- `opsgenie`<br>|
|» integration_id|body|integer|false|ID of the integration used as the notification service. See<br>[List Integrations](https://docs.sentry.io/api/integrations/list-an-organizations-available-integrations/)<br>to retrieve a full list of integrations.<br><br>Required if **service_type** is `slack`, `pagerduty` or `opsgenie`.<br>|
|» target_identifier|body|string|false|ID of the notification target, like a Slack channel ID.<br><br>Required if **service_type** is `slack` or `opsgenie`.<br>|
|» target_display|body|string|false|Name of the notification target, like a Slack channel name.<br><br>Required if **service_type** is `slack` or `opsgenie`.<br>|
|» projects|body|[string]|false|List of project IDs or slugs that the Notification Action is created for.|
|» sentry_app_id|body|integer|false|ID of the custom integration to notify, when the target is a Sentry app.|
|» target_type|body|string|false|How the notification target is addressed.|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": 836501735,
  "organizationId": 62848264,
  "integrationId": null,
  "sentryAppId": null,
  "serviceType": "sentry_notification",
  "targetDisplay": "default",
  "targetIdentifier": "default",
  "targetType": "specific",
  "triggerType": "spike-protection",
  "projects": [
    4505321021243392
  ]
}
```

|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|

Status Code **201**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|id|integer|true|none|ID of the notification action|
|organizationId|integer|true|none|ID of the organization|

|sentryAppId|integer \| null|true|none|ID of the Sentry app that receives the notification. Null when none is used|
|projects|[integer]|true|none|IDs of the projects the action applies to|

curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/available-actions/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/available-actions/`

**Experimental:** This API is under active development and may change.

Returns a list of available actions for a given org

<h3 id="list-available-alert-actions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|type|query|[string]|false|Filter by action type. Can be specified multiple times.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|type|discord|
|type|email|
|type|github|
|type|github_enterprise|
|type|jira|
|type|jira_server|
|type|msteams|
|type|opsgenie|
|type|pagerduty|
|type|seer_workflow|
|type|sentry_app|
|type|slack|
|type|slack_staging|
|type|vsts|
|type|webhook|

## Fetch an Organization's Monitors

<a id="opIdlistOrganizationDetectors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/detectors/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/detectors/`

List an Organization's Monitors

<h3 id="fetch-an-organizations-monitors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|query|query|string|false|An optional search query for filtering monitors.<br><br>Available fields are:<br>- `name`<br>- `type`: e.g. `error`, `metric_issue`, `issue_stream`<br>- `assignee`: email, username, #team, me, none<br>        |
|sortBy|query|string|false|The property to sort results by. If not specified, the results are sorted by id.<br><br>Available fields are:<br>- `name`<br>- `id`<br>- `type`<br>- `connectedWorkflows`<br>- `latestGroup`<br>- `openIssues`<br><br>Prefix with `-` to sort in descending order.<br>        |
|id|query|[integer]|false|The ID of the monitor you'd like to query.|
|type|query|[string]|false|Filter by monitor type(s). Can be specified multiple times.|
|enabled|query|boolean|false|Filter by whether monitors are enabled.|
|per_page|query|integer|false|Limit the number of rows to return in the result. Default and maximum allowed is 100.|
|cursor|query|string|false|A pointer to the last object fetched and its sort order; used to retrieve the next or previous results.|

## Mutate an Organization's Monitors

<a id="opIdupdateOrganizationDetectors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/detectors/' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "enabled": true
  }'
```

`PUT /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/detectors/`

Bulk enable or disable an Organization's Monitors

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "enabled": true
}
```

<h3 id="mutate-an-organizations-monitors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|query|query|string|false|An optional search query for filtering monitors.<br><br>Available fields are:<br>- `name`<br>- `type`: e.g. `error`, `metric_issue`, `issue_stream`<br>- `assignee`: email, username, #team, me, none<br>        |
|id|query|[integer]|false|The ID of the monitor you'd like to query.|
|body|body|object|true|none|
|» enabled|body|boolean|true|Whether to enable or disable the monitors|

<h3 id="mutate-an-organizations-monitors-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK||Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<h3 id="mutate-an-organizations-monitors-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anonymous*|[object]|false|none|none|
|» owner|object \| null|false|none|Team or user that owns the monitor|
|» » type|string|true|none|Whether the actor is a user or a team|
|» » id|string|true|none|ID of the user or team|
|» » name|string|true|none|Display name of the user, or slug of the team|
|» » email|string|false|none|Email address of the user. Only set for users|
|» createdBy|string \| null|false|none|ID of the user who created the monitor|
|» latestGroup|object \| null|false|none|Latest issue the monitor created|
|» » id|string|true|none|ID of the issue|
|» » title|string|true|none|Title of the issue|
|» » culprit|string \| null|true|none|Function or module where the issue occurs|
|» » shortId|string \| null|true|none|Short ID of the issue, such as PROJECT-1A|
|» » level|string|true|none|Severity level of the issue|
|» » status|string|true|none|Issue status|
|» » substatus|string \| null|true|none|Substatus of the issue, such as ongoing, regressed or escalating|
|» » platform|string \| null|true|none|Platform of the issue's events|
|» » project|object|true|none|Project the issue belongs to|
|» » » id|string|true|none|ID of the project|
|» » » name|string|true|none|Name of the project|
|» » » slug|string|true|none|Slug of the project|
|» » » platform|string \| null|true|none|Platform of the project|
|» » type|string|true|none|Event type of the issue, such as error or default|
|» » issueType|string|true|none|Issue type, such as error or performance_n_plus_one_db_queries|
|» » issueCategory|string|true|none|Issue category, such as error or performance|
|» » metadata|object|true|none|Issue metadata|
|» » » title|string|false|none|Title of default and issue platform events|
|» » » value|string|false|none|Exception value, or the subtitle of an issue|
|» » » type|string|false|none|Exception type of error events|

## Bulk Delete Monitors

<a id="opIddeleteOrganizationDetectors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/detectors/' \
  -X DELETE \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/detectors/`

Bulk delete Monitors for a given organization

<h3 id="bulk-delete-monitors-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|project|query|[integer \| string]|false|The IDs or slugs of projects to filter by. Project slugs are unique within each organization. Omit this parameter to include all accessible projects. `-1` is also accepted to include all accessible projects.<br>For example, the following are valid parameters:<br>- `/?project=1234&project=56789`<br>- `/?project=android&project=javascript-react`<br>- `/?project=-1`<br>|
|query|query|string|false|An optional search query for filtering monitors.<br><br>Available fields are:<br>- `name`<br>- `type`: e.g. `error`, `metric_issue`, `issue_stream`<br>- `assignee`: email, username, #team, me, none<br>        |
|sortBy|query|string|false|The property to sort results by. If not specified, the results are sorted by id.<br><br>Available fields are:<br>- `name`<br>- `id`<br>- `type`<br>- `connectedWorkflows`<br>- `latestGroup`<br>- `openIssues`<br><br>Prefix with `-` to sort in descending order.<br>        |
|id|query|[integer]|false|The ID of the monitor you'd like to query.|

<h3 id="bulk-delete-monitors-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Success|None|
|204|No Content|No Content|None|
|400|Bad Request|Bad Request|None|
|401|Unauthorized|Unauthorized|None|
|403|Forbidden|Forbidden|None|
|404|Not Found|Not Found|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
auth_token
</aside>

## Fetch a Monitor

<a id="opIdgetOrganizationDetector"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://{region}.sentry.io/organizations/string/detectors/0/' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /organizations/{organization_id_or_slug}/detectors/{detector_id}/`

Return details on an individual monitor

<h3 id="fetch-a-monitor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|organization_id_or_slug|path|string|true|The ID or slug of the organization the resource belongs to.|
|detector_id|path|integer|true|The ID of the monitor you'd like to query.|
